title: Specify needs
description: This phase is triggered when a need for new statistics is identified, perhaps resulting from user feedback, or a review is undertaken. It includes all activities associated with engaging stakeholders to identify their detailed statistical needs (current or future), proposing high level solution options, and preparing a business case. In the modernized statistical environment, these activities are increasingly supported by automated and AI-powered processes—ranging from the synthesis and structuring of stakeholder inputs, through the analysis of options, to the automated drafting of business case materials. Routine and repetitive aspects of needs identification, consultation, and documentation are minimized for manual intervention, enabling staff to focus on higher-value tasks: interpreting context, establishing priorities, and making strategic decisions that cannot be automated. The phase thus leverages end-to-end process automation and AI wherever possible, supporting greater efficiency, responsiveness, and quality at the earliest stage of the statistical business process. The Specify Needs phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 7), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because it centers on identifying stakeholder statistical needs, assessing current and future requirements, analyzing options, and supporting business-case style justification for new or modified statistical activity. That requires roles able to engage clients and stakeholders, gather and synthesize qualitative and quantitative information, assess requirements, and contribute analytical input on feasibility or impacts. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fits these needs because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data," "identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data," and has communication responsibilities to "establish and maintain positive relations with Statistics Canada clients and stakeholders within and outside the Agency" and to participate in "interviews, and focus groups." The role also supports option and case analysis through "socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis of programs" and preparation of "reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because specifying needs requires translating stakeholder and program requirements into structured specifications, especially where new statistics or modified programs are being considered. That requires a role able to interpret client requirements, assess impacts of changes, and propose enhancements or alternatives. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer is directly relevant because the role "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications" and "interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata." It also "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives," which aligns with the phase's need to propose high-level solution options.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because identifying needs for new statistics depends on gathering information from stakeholders, understanding data requirements, and translating subject-matter needs into specifications for future development. That requires analytical support, stakeholder engagement, and knowledge of the data life cycle and governance. The Junior Data Analyst fits this because the role attends "interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information," and "discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur." The role also "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development" and has knowledge of "data science and its life cycle" and methods needed to assess data quality and support decision-making.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because specifying needs includes understanding operational implications, consulting users and service providers, and outlining options and requirements for how future statistical operations could work. That requires a role that can engage stakeholders, understand operational conditions, and prepare recommendations on requirements. The Operations Officer is relevant because the role "meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur" and "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems." The role also "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," which supports the phase's emphasis on high-level solution options.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because specifying needs requires subject-matter review, feasibility and impact thinking for new or modified statistical programs, and translation of user requirements into plans and specifications. That requires a role with knowledge of program context, emerging issues, and feasibility assessment. Economist/Sociologist 2 fits because the role "participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers," has knowledge of "methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs," and "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates." These are directly aligned with identifying needs and shaping response options.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because stakeholder needs specification includes interpreting user information requests, understanding feasibility and options, and considering the potential impact of new or modified statistical programs. That requires a role that works directly with users and assesses requests in terms of possible outputs and program implications. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is implicated because the role "interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," "provides statistical data and consultative services to users," and has knowledge of "methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs." The role also "interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required," which closely matches the needs-identification and options-analysis aspects of this phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Identify needs
description: This sub-process includes the initial investigation and identification of what statistics are needed and what is needed of the statistics. In the modern process, AI and automated tools are used to continuously scan for new information requests from users, detect relevant environmental changes, and aggregate respondent feedback and evaluation action plans. These technologies also benchmark needs by automatically referencing practices among other (national and international) statistical organizations. Automation supports the collation, analysis, and structuring of these triggers for new or changed statistics, while staff focus their expertise on interpreting context, confirming significance, and ensuring response to complex or emergent requirements.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires the initial investigation of user needs, identification of new information requests, interpretation of respondent feedback, and assessment of what statistics are needed or need to change. That requires capability to gather requirements from clients and stakeholders, research and synthesize qualitative and quantitative information, and help assess current and future data requirements. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fills this need because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," and also "undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as... identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data" and participates in "interviews, and focus groups." The role also has communication responsibilities to "discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues" and to participate in discussions with clients on "data requirements," which directly supports identifying needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying needs includes translating user and program requirements into structured specifications, understanding changing information demands, and interpreting what is needed of the statistics. That requires capability to gather data requirements, liaise with stakeholders, organize information relevant to study objectives, and apply data-science methods to evolving information sources. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information," and "as assigned, discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur." It also "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development" and has knowledge of "evolving information sources" and methods of information collection and analysis, which are directly relevant to identifying emerging statistical needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying needs includes detecting relevant environmental changes, identifying trends and developments, and suggesting where statistical programs or methods may need to change in response to user or contextual demands. That requires subject-matter analysis, awareness of emerging economic and social issues, and the ability to translate subject-matter requirements into program specifications. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "identifies statistical trends and developments," "participates in subject matter studies and reviews," and "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs." The role also has knowledge of "current and emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series" and of methods to "develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs," which directly supports identifying needs for new or changed statistics.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying needs includes interpreting user information requests and determining the nature and feasibility of statistical outputs required. That requires direct engagement with users, interpretation of requests, and assessment of the potential impact of new or modified statistical programs. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," "provides statistical data and consultative services to users," and "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs." Its research and analysis explicitly include "interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required" and knowledge of "methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs," making it directly relevant to identifying statistical needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying needs also involves understanding operational conditions, respondent issues, and changes in data sources or subject areas that may trigger new or changed statistics. That requires engagement with clients and respondents, analysis of changes affecting outputs, and articulation of operational requirements. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur," and "contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration... to clarify problems or irregularities." The role also "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results" and has knowledge of "developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing," which supports identifying needs arising from operational and environmental change.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying needs includes understanding what metadata and documentation are required by programs and clients when statistics are created or changed, and translating those requirements into specifications. That requires interpreting client requirements, liaising with survey managers and subject matter specialists, and assessing program metadata requirements across statistical programs. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," and "interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata." It also has knowledge of "surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to understand program statistical metadata requirements," which is directly relevant when identifying what is needed of the statistics.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Consult and confirm needs
description: This sub-process focuses on consulting with internal and external stakeholders and confirming in detail the needs for the statistics. Automated and AI-supported systems are now used to organize and analyze input from stakeholders, including feedback, evolving requirements, and historical engagement. These tools facilitate discovery of patterns and highlight changes in user needs over time. Statistical staff engage directly where nuanced negotiation, detailed interpretation, or complex prioritization is required, ensuring that automated summaries and analytics are supplemented by expert, context-aware judgment. This detailed understanding of user needs and the efficient, technology-enabled consultation process are both critical to this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on consulting stakeholders, interpreting and confirming detailed statistical needs, and translating those needs into actionable specifications, often where nuanced negotiation and prioritization are required. That requires a role able to liaise with users, interpret requests, and convert requirements into specifications. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the work-description states that the position "Provides statistical data and consultative services to users," "Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," and "Liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because confirming needs depends on direct engagement with stakeholders, gathering information in meetings, and elaborating the conditions under which statistical work will occur. That requires a role that can discuss data requirements with clients and subject-matter specialists and help translate those needs into operational terms. The Junior Data Analyst is directly relevant because the work-description says the position "Attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information," "discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur," and "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because consultation and confirmation of needs require engagement with users and subject-matter specialists to develop, translate, and negotiate requirements, including procedural modifications and priorities. That requires a role with explicit responsibility for liaising with users and helping establish plans and priorities. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fits this need because the work-description states that the position "Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates." This directly matches the phase emphasis on nuanced interpretation and complex prioritization of user needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because stakeholder consultation often includes understanding operational conditions, resolving differences, and obtaining collaboration from respondents or data suppliers so that needs are clearly confirmed and feasible. That requires a role experienced in meeting with clients and service providers and clarifying issues affecting operations and outputs. The Operations Officer is implicated because the work-description says the position "Meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur" and must "understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs." It also notes contact with "data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration" and to "clarify and explain statistical concepts."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because confirming needs includes understanding and translating client requirements in a specialized domain, here statistical metadata, and negotiating priorities and procedural modifications with internal stakeholders. That requires a role that liaises with clients and interprets requirements into specifications. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the work-description states that the position "Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; to negotiate procedural modifications, priorities and target dates," and "Interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because consultation with stakeholders and confirmation of needs can require interviews, focus groups, discussion of data requirements, and synthesis of qualitative and quantitative input. That requires a role able to gather stakeholder input and analyze requirements, even under supervision. The Junior Evaluation Officer is relevant because the work-description states that the position undertakes tasks such as "identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups," "Provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data," and has communication responsibilities to "discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients" and to "participate in interviews, focus groups and discussions with Statistics Canada clients on data requirements."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Establish output objectives
description: This sub-process identifies the statistical output objectives that are required to meet the user needs confirmed in sub-process 1.2 (Consult and confirm needs). AI and automated tools aggregate and analyze confirmed user requirements, historical deliverables, legal/normative frameworks, and available resource constraints to generate draft output objectives and candidate quality measures. Staff provide oversight by aligning these drafts with strategic intent, adjudicating complex trade-offs, and ensuring compliance with legal and methodological expectations. This shift supports more efficient, responsive, and high-quality output objective-setting by leveraging technology for foundational work and human expertise for final judgment and alignment.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires translating confirmed user needs into concrete statistical output objectives, while also weighing historical outputs, resource constraints, and legal/methodological expectations. That creates a need for roles that can interpret user requirements, assess feasibility and impact of modified statistical programs, and help translate subject-matter requirements into specifications. The Economist/Sociologist 2 directly fills this need because it "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and has "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs." It also analyzes how changes in methodology and procedures affect "data output, products and services," which is central to establishing realistic output objectives.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because draft output objectives must be aligned to user needs and converted into practical output products and services, with attention to feasibility, data quality, and dissemination implications. That requires a role able to interpret user requests, assess options for outputs, and evaluate effects of procedural or system changes on products and services. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because it "interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," "provides statistical data and consultative services to users," and has research responsibilities to "interpret user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required." It also "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services," directly supporting the setting of output objectives.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because establishing output objectives includes defining candidate quality measures and ensuring outputs are documented and aligned with standards, policies, and dissemination requirements. That creates a need for expertise in metadata requirements, quality evaluation, and policy-compliant documentation of outputs. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because it "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." It also has knowledge of "policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata" and "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations," which supports defining output objectives and associated quality measures in a compliant and standardized way.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because AI-generated draft output objectives depend on analysis of user requirements, historical deliverables, and constraints, and staff must assess evidence and support decisions with structured analysis. That requires capability in organizing information relevant to defined objectives, assessing data quality, and supporting analytical work that informs decision-making. The Junior Data Analyst supports this need because it "organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies," has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "summarization, reporting, visualization" and "exploratory/ confirmatory, predictive analysis," and can "assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity." This makes the role directly relevant to evidence-based drafting and refinement of output objectives.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because output objectives must be realistic in light of available resource constraints and operational conditions, and must account for how collection and processing systems can support the intended outputs. That creates a need for operational analysis of requirements, options, and impacts on statistical operations and output quality. The Operations Officer fills this need because it "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems," meets with specialists and clients "to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur," and "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results." This operational perspective is directly implicated in setting achievable output objectives.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because staff oversight must adjudicate trade-offs among user needs, strategic intent, and resource constraints, which requires evaluative analysis of requirements, data needs, and implications for outputs. The Junior Evaluation Officer contributes to this need through support for assessing requirements and analyzing evidence. The work description states that the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases" and "undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as... identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data." It also includes "knowledge of program evaluation and performance measurement theories, processes and practices," which is relevant when candidate quality measures and output objectives are being established.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Identify concepts
description: This sub-process clarifies the required concepts to be measured from the point of view of the users. Automated and AI-assisted tools are leveraged to synthesize user requirements, prior documentation, and relevant internal/external sources, providing preliminary suggestions and structured options for possible concepts. The role of the subject matter sponsor is central—this person or group is solely accountable for the final specification and formal certification of the required concepts prior to downstream design or standard alignment. This approach minimizes manual tasks, maintains clear accountability, and increases speed and efficiency in the establishment of robust conceptual frameworks.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it focuses on clarifying and specifying the concepts to be measured from the users’ point of view, which requires subject-matter capability to translate user needs into formal conceptual specifications and assess the implications of alternative concepts. This needs a role that can work with users and other specialists to turn subject-matter requirements into specifications and assess the impact of different concepts, definitions and conditions. Economist/Sociologist 2 fits this need because it explicitly "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and has the ability to "assess and determine the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored." It also has "knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey" and of "methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying concepts depends on understanding user requirements, synthesizing information from multiple sources, and translating those requirements into structured specifications for downstream work. This requires analytical support to gather information, discuss requirements with clients and specialists, and help elaborate the conditions under which statistical development will occur. Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information," "discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur," and "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development." Its knowledge of "data science and its life cycle" and "techniques and methods of information collection and analysis" supports synthesis of user requirements and source material.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because concept identification must be grounded in metadata and documented standards so that proposed concepts are clearly defined and can later align with formal statistical metadata frameworks. This requires a role able to interpret client requirements, advise on metadata concepts and frameworks, and translate requirements into specifications. Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because it "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," and has "knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally." The role also "interprets client requirements in order to determine options" and can provide "assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," which is directly relevant when clarifying and formalizing concepts.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because identifying concepts from the users’ perspective requires gathering and synthesizing evidence from literature, data, interviews, focus groups, and stakeholder discussions to clarify what should be measured. This requires a role that can research requirements, synthesize qualitative and quantitative inputs, and support conclusions about what concepts are needed. Junior Evaluation Officer fits this need because it "undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups," and "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data." The role also has speaking skills "to discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues" and participates in meetings "to discuss files / issues and evaluation requirements," which supports user-oriented concept clarification.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because concept identification requires understanding how subject-matter requirements from users will be expressed in program outputs and translated into specifications for ongoing statistical programs. This needs a role that can work with users, interpret subject-matter concepts, and assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs. Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because it "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs." It also has "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs" and "interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required," all of which support the structured identification of concepts.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because once concepts are being identified, operational implications must also be understood so that concepts can be explained consistently to respondents and implemented in collection and processing environments. This requires a role with knowledge of statistical concepts and experience elaborating operational conditions with subject matter and systems specialists. Operations Officer fits this need because it meets with "subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur," and may need "to clarify and explain statistical concepts." The role also has "knowledge of the underlying statistical and economic principles and concepts required for the collection, coding and processing of data" and prepares reports on "problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions," which makes it relevant to concept identification where operational viability matters.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Check data availability and suitability
description: This sub-process systematically checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available, including any restrictions on their use. Existing data holdings must be exhaustively investigated and prioritized first, followed by a search for relevant administrative and alternative data sources; the option to conduct new surveys is only considered if these avenues prove insufficient to meet data needs. The subject matter sponsor holds sole accountability for certifying that all relevant avenues for data have been thoroughly explored and that the suitability, timeliness, and quality of any proposed source have been rigorously assessed. To expedite and strengthen the acquisition of administrative and alternative data, a center of expertise works collaboratively with subject matter specialists to support negotiations, acquisition logistics, and the establishment of legal or operational agreements where needed. When multiple avenues have been assessed and documented, a strategy for filling any remaining gaps is prepared. This sub-process also encompasses the assessment and possible updates to the legal framework for data collection, ensuring fit-for-purpose, respondent-efficient, and timely data acquisition and usage.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires a systematic assessment of whether existing, administrative, and alternative data sources can meet user requirements, including evaluating accessibility, restrictions, quality, timeliness, and suitability before any new collection is considered. That requires capability to identify useful and accessible sources, gather and analyze data from multiple sources, discuss data requirements with clients, and support data acquisition. This work description fits that need because it explicitly states the role 'provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases' and 'identifies and recommends ... the usefulness and accessible sources of data to be used in studies.' It also notes communication with clients 'in the data acquisition process' and obtaining data from 'outside professionals,' which aligns with checking availability and suitability of candidate sources.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because checking data availability and suitability depends on understanding source documentation, metadata quality, standards, and legal/policy constraints governing use of data. That requires capability to interpret requirements for metadata, evaluate metadata quality, and apply policies and legislation such as the Statistics Act and Privacy Act. This work description fills that need because it 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations,' 'interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' and has 'knowledge of the Statistics Act and of Statistics Canada policies, directives and guidelines' as well as 'awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information.' Those elements directly support assessing whether a source is sufficiently documented, usable, and legally suitable.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires technical assessment of candidate data sources for origin, quality, conformity to standards, integrity, and the conditions under which they can be used in statistical development. That requires capability in data acquisition, extraction, validation, quality assessment, and discussion of data requirements with operational and subject-matter partners. This work description fills that need because it includes 'data capture and acquisition,' 'data extraction,' 'data cleansing,' 'data transformation,' 'data validation,' 'ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' and states that the incumbent may 'discuss data requirements with operations managers ... subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur.' It also includes knowledge of 'data risk assessment' and assessing data from partners 'for validity and integrity,' which is central to suitability review.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because assessing data availability and suitability includes examining operational feasibility of collection or acquisition methods, understanding data sources and supplier contacts, evaluating changes to sources, and respecting legal restrictions on collection and use. That requires capability to evaluate collection methods and results, work with data suppliers, and analyze impacts of source changes on integrity and completeness. This work description fills that need because it 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' 'meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur,' and 'contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration.' It also includes 'knowledge of data sources and contacts within Statistics Canada ... and external ... to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information' and 'knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts,' directly supporting source availability, acquisition conditions, and legal framework considerations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the phase centers on determining whether available sources are relevant to subject-matter requirements and whether the conditions of collection, processing, and storage affect the validity and usability of the data. That requires subject-matter capability to assess feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs, understand respondents and sponsors, and analyze constraints arising from concepts, definitions, and collection conditions. This work description fills that need because it includes 'knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs,' 'knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents,' and the ability to 'assess and determine the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.' It also notes 'knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada,' which directly supports exhaustive investigation of existing holdings.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because checking data availability and suitability requires reviewing candidate data sources for validity, consistency, reliability, appropriateness, and feasibility of meeting user requests, including adapting data from multiple sources. That requires capability to assess data quality from systems and databases, interpret user requirements, and analyze source impacts on outputs and services. This work description fills that need because it 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' 'interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required,' and 'compiles data from diverse sources' while 'analyz[ing] and evaluat[ing] data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness.' It also includes 'knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures ... to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs' and knowledge of the Statistics Act and related policies, which supports both suitability assessment and use restrictions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Prepare and submit business case
description: This sub-process documents the findings of the other sub-processes in this phase in the form of a business case to get approval to implement a new or modified statistical business process. In the contemporary process, automated and AI-driven systems are used to collate, analyze, and generate initial drafts for all key business case sections—including the description of the 'As-Is' process, the proposed 'To-Be' solution, and the relevant assessments of cost, benefit, risks, deliverables, and impact. Staff and sponsors then review, contextualize, and refine these drafts, ensuring proper alignment with strategic objectives and organizational needs before final submission. The business case is reviewed and approved by the relevant body, with human expertise providing the final evaluation and decision. By leveraging automation, the preparation of business cases gains efficiency and speed, allowing human effort to be concentrated on strategic oversight and quality assurance.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires documenting findings from earlier work into a formal business case, including assessments of cost, benefit, risks, deliverables, impact, and alignment with organizational needs before approval of a new or modified statistical business process. That creates a need for capability in evaluation, socio-economic and cost-benefit analysis, synthesis of evidence, and preparation of briefing/report material for senior management. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fills this need because the role 'participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies related to programs, policies and initiatives,' 'provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data,' and specifically 'participates in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis of programs.' The role also 'provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management,' which closely matches preparing the documented business case for review and approval.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the business case must assemble and analyze evidence about the current state ('As-Is'), proposed future state ('To-Be'), impacts, risks, and strategic fit, often using automated and AI-driven collation and analysis. That requires data analysis capability, data preparation, risk and impact assessment, and preparation of analytical briefings and presentations for decision-makers. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role 'supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods,' performs 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' and has knowledge of 'data science and its life cycle' including 'reporting, visualization, business intelligence.' The work description also explicitly includes 'data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis' and states that writing skills are needed 'to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material,' which is directly relevant to drafting and refining a business case.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because a business case for a new or modified statistical business process must explain operational implications of the current and proposed processes, identify requirements, and assess impacts on collection, coding, processing systems, and operational efficiency. That creates a need for operational analysis, requirements articulation, and preparation of reports and recommendations on options. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' 'prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems,' and 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.' The role also 'analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results,' which supports the business case sections on impacts, risks, and the transition from As-Is to To-Be operations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because preparing a business case for a new or modified statistical process requires assessing feasibility, impact, procedural changes, and implications for statistical programs, then translating those findings into plans, priorities, and management-oriented documentation. That creates a need for subject-matter analysis of modified programs and their impacts. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role includes 'knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.' It also 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development' and 'writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports.' In research and analysis, the role 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems,' which directly supports documenting As-Is and To-Be states in a business case.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the business case must review the feasibility and potential impact of proposed changes, interpret requirements, and assess effects on outputs, products, and services before approval. That creates a need for analytical support on feasibility, impact, user requirements, and implications of revised processing specifications. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role has 'knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs.' The role also 'interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required,' and 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' These responsibilities directly support business case sections on options, impacts, deliverables, and implications of the proposed To-Be process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because a business case for a modified statistical business process may need to document metadata implications of the As-Is and To-Be designs, assess impacts of changed methods and systems, and provide supporting documentation for management review. That creates a need for capability to interpret requirements, analyze impacts of modified methods and procedures, and contribute to documentation and reporting. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role 'liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications,' 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata,' and 'analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives.' The role also 'contributes written information to be used as input to reports' and documentation, which supports preparation of business case material where metadata changes are part of the proposed process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Design
description: This phase describes the development and design activities, and any associated practical research work needed to define the statistical outputs, variables, methodologies, collection instruments, and operational processes—with a strong emphasis on automation, AI-powered tools, and digital interoperability. Automated and AI-driven processes play a central role in drafting specifications, aligning with corporate and international standards, generating and enriching metadata, simulating system interactions, and iterating design improvements. All statistical products and their supporting metadata are produced in standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable forms, ensuring they are interoperable and reusable across downstream tools, APIs, and organizational systems. Staff are freed from repetitive and routine design work and instead focus on innovation, calibration, and optimizing for evolving user and stakeholder requirements. Design activities thus promote efficiency, quality, and discoverability, embedding best practices for automation, standardization, and open data access. The Design phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 8), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, can occur in parallel, and may be iterative. Iteration between Design and Build phases is supported through automated versioning and process enhancements.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because it centers on defining statistical outputs, variables, methodologies, collection instruments, operational processes, and standardized machine-actionable metadata and specifications. That requires capability to develop and translate requirements into metadata specifications, align with standards and policies, test new procedures and systems, and support metadata quality and interoperability. This work-description directly fills that need because it "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," and "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." It also explicitly supports design iteration through participation in "testing of new procedures and systems" and analysis of "current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because design requires defining data structures, variables, methods, and specifications for downstream statistical development and operations, with emphasis on standards, quality, and evolving user requirements. That requires capability to translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for data development, assess data quality and conformity to standards, and recommend methodologies. This work-description fills that need because it "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development." It also brings methodological design support through "basic knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of research... model design and interpretation, experimental and comparative study designs; surveys, simulations" and the ability "to recommend and select project methodologies."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because design includes defining collection instruments and operational processes and drafting specifications for how collection, coding, and processing will work in practice. That requires capability in operational design, evaluation of collection and coding methods, and specification of testing and processing requirements. This work-description fills that need because it "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems." It is especially relevant to design-build iteration because it has "knowledge of systems analysis and design... for designing the specifications for testing of applications" and "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because design requires developing and refining statistical methodologies, concepts, definitions, outputs, and system specifications in response to subject-matter needs and changing requirements. That requires capability to analyze and propose changes to collection, processing, editing, compilation, and presentation methods and to translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications. This work-description fills that need because it "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs," and has knowledge of "methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs." It directly supports design improvement because it "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because design includes defining statistical outputs and ensuring that system and processing specifications support intended products, services, and user needs. That requires capability to translate user and subject-matter requirements into system specifications, assess impacts of new or revised processing specifications, and adapt outputs to new definitions or formats. This work-description fills that need because it "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs." It also supports design of outputs and interoperability by "examining operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems" and by adapting "data to new definitions or presentation formats."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because design includes practical research work to define outputs, methodologies, and stakeholder requirements, and to optimize design choices based on evidence. That requires capability to assess data requirements, conduct literature and data research, analyze qualitative and quantitative evidence, and recommend enhancements to methods. This work-description fills that need because it "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data," "undertakes literature and data research," and "recommends to the Evaluation Manager, enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analyses." While not a primary design-production role, it is directly relevant to the research and requirements-definition aspects of the phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Design outputs and dissemination
description: This sub-process contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products, and services to be produced, including all systems, tools, and procedures to be used in dissemination. Automated and AI-supported solutions are used wherever possible to produce initial output templates, align with existing standards, generate metadata, and configure dissemination tools, allowing staff to focus on innovative features and context-specific requirements, including confidentiality. All outputs and dissemination artifacts must be standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable, with support for APIs, comprehensive metadata tagging, and open formats to maximize interoperability, discoverability, and reusability by human and machine clients. The process includes an explicit, early review of the type and necessity of products, especially visualizations, with the expectation that only those genuinely required for user value or compliance are designed—allowing exclusion where end-users can self-serve or alternatives suffice. Outputs may also be designed in partnership with external organizations, ensuring full alignment with digital-to-digital workflows and standards.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly covers the detailed design of outputs, products, services, dissemination systems and tools, and requires outputs to be standardized, machine-actionable, metadata-rich, and designed for user value and confidentiality. That creates a need for a role that directly works on dissemination products, interprets user requests, adapts outputs to presentation formats, and contributes to dissemination practices. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' and 'Participates on data production and dissemination teams.' Its analytical duties also align with output design because it 'Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' 'Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required,' and 'Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats.' The confidentiality aspect is also covered through awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires dissemination artifacts to be 'richly described,' 'machine-actionable,' and supported by 'comprehensive metadata tagging,' with alignment to standards, open formats, and dissemination tools. That creates a need for a role specifically responsible for producing, validating, disseminating, and evaluating statistical metadata and for translating requirements into metadata specifications. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.' It also 'provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines,' and 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata.' The role is especially relevant to standards-based dissemination because it has knowledge of 'statistical metadata concepts and frameworks' and of methods and systems for 'producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata,' while also recognizing confidentiality through 'awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes the detailed design of statistical outputs and products, including review of which products and visualizations are genuinely needed, and requires alignment between subject-matter requirements and dissemination specifications. That creates a need for a role that analyzes effects on 'data output, products and services,' helps translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications, and contributes to presentation methods. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills that need because the role 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes,' and liaises 'to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development.' It is directly tied to output design through research activities that 'Analyze changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and 'Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' The role also supports compliant presentation through awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes designing dissemination systems, tools, procedures, and output artifacts such as tables, charts, graphs, and explanatory text, while ensuring outputs remain reliable and aligned with operational realities. That creates a need for a role that prepares publication-oriented output artifacts and assesses how changes to outputs affect program results and operational systems. The Operations Officer fills that need because the role 'Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications.' It also supports dissemination-system design by 'Prepar[ing] reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems' and by meeting with specialists and clients 'to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur.' Its research responsibilities are relevant because it 'Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.' The confidentiality requirement is also supported through awareness of 'the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it emphasizes output templates, visualizations, user-oriented products, and machine-actionable dissemination artifacts, which creates a need for capability in reporting, visualization, and translating analytical requirements into specifications. The Junior Data Analyst helps fill that need because the role supports the data life cycle including 'summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence,' and has 'data literacy' needed to 'read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data.' The role is also relevant to designing dissemination-ready products because it uses writing skills 'to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science.' In addition, it can help translate requirements into output specifications because it 'liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Design variables
description: This sub-process defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument and any that will be derived for analysis or dissemination, with a strong emphasis on standards compliance, automation, and machine-actionability. All variable definitions and supporting metadata must comply with national and international standards (e.g., SDMX), structured in machine-actionable formats and managed through prescribed data management tools (such as Aria or Colectica) to ensure robust lifecycle control and digital traceability. AI/LLM-enabled tools are used to generate, refine, and validate variable names, descriptions, and attributes, maximizing clarity, standardization, and discoverability. Staff involved in this sub-process are proficient in digital metadata standards and tooling, ensuring all variable-related products are interoperable, automation-ready, and reusable by both human and machine users. This ensures that the resulting statistical outputs are consistently described, easily found, and seamlessly integrated across digital platforms and systems.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is directly implicated because it centers on defining variables and their supporting metadata in standards-compliant, machine-actionable forms, and on managing them through metadata tools and procedures. That requires capability in statistical metadata concepts, standards, validation, storage, dissemination, quality evaluation, and advising clients on metadata requirements. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," and has "knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally" as well as "knowledge of software used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." The role also "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," which aligns closely with defining variables and their metadata for interoperable, automation-ready use.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicated because designing variables requires translating subject-matter requirements into formal specifications, ensuring concepts, definitions, and variables are suitable for collection, processing, analysis, and dissemination. That requires subject-matter knowledge, ability to assess concepts and definitions, and experience proposing changes to methods and specifications. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and "writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology." It also includes "knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey" and the ability to "assess and determine the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored," which is directly relevant to defining variables appropriately.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicated because variable design must support downstream data capture, transformation, validation, standards conformity, and analytical use, including derived variables for analysis and dissemination. That requires data lifecycle knowledge, standards awareness, and the ability to translate requirements into specifications for data development. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role conducts "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and has "knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing... summarization, reporting." The role also "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development," which supports the design of variables that are usable in automated and analytical workflows.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicated because variables must be defined for use in collection instruments and operational systems, with attention to how concepts and definitions will function in collection, coding, and processing environments. That requires operational knowledge of collection and processing specifications, data flows, and the effects of concepts and definitions on implementation quality. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding," and has "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" for "designing the specifications for testing of applications." The role also "analyses reported data and work results... presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions," which is directly relevant when designing variables for collection instruments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicated because variables are not only collected but also derived for analysis or dissemination, so their definitions must support valid outputs, adaptation to formats, and user-facing statistical products. That requires understanding of data validity, output requirements, and how specifications affect dissemination products. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "provides statistical data and consultative services to users," and "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development." The role also "adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats" and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions," which supports designing variables that will work for dissemination and derived outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Design collection
