description: This sub-process prepares a collection strategy for the data and determines the most appropriate collection instruments and methods, with a strategic emphasis on automation, AI/ML, and passive acquisition. Where possible, the design must prioritize passive, administrative, and already-available sources of data; surveys or direct solicitation are employed only when all other avenues are exhausted or cannot provide suitable data. All aspects of collection design—including the configuration of instruments, sequencing, respondent communications, and integration agreements—should embed automation, machine-to-machine interfaces, digital event/trigger-based collection, and minimal manual intervention. Where a survey instrument is essential, automated and AI-driven methods must be used for design, rendering, and fielding, ensuring quick turnaround, reduced burden, and full standards compliance. The sub-process also entails the necessary design of respondent management, monitoring, and adaptive feedback loops to maximize efficiency and data quality, while reserving human staff for exception handling and final validation.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is explicitly about designing collection strategy, instruments, methods, respondent communications, monitoring, and automated operational flows. That requires capability in collection operations, evaluating collection methods, specifying operational requirements, and documenting procedures and training for collection. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding." The role also supports the design and operationalization of collection systems through "prepar[ing] reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems," writing "survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures," and using knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" and of developments affecting "the efficiency and validity of data collection."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because collection design must determine the most appropriate instruments and methods, prioritize passive and administrative sources, and embed automation and machine-to-machine interfaces. That requires capability to translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications, assess collection methodologies, and analyze alternative collection procedures. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," has knowledge of "methods and techniques of data gathering," and "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs." It is also directly tied to improving collection design because it "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures" and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because designing collection in an automated, AI/ML-enabled, low-burden way requires data-method expertise across the data life cycle, including capture, acquisition, quality assessment, survey methodologies, and translation of operational requirements into specifications. Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role has knowledge of "data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition," as well as "data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing" and advanced analytical methods. The role also has "knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies, data risk assessment" and can "discuss data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur." In addition, it "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development," which supports the design of automated collection instruments and interfaces.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because collection design must ensure that instruments, respondent communications, and automated collection processes are standards-compliant and properly documented, especially when surveys remain necessary. That requires metadata expertise to translate requirements into specifications and to support methods, procedures, systems, and standards used across collection programs. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." The role also has "knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data" and "knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks... reflected in policies, methods and procedures." This supports standards compliance and documentation for collection instruments and processes, and the role further contributes by providing feedback on "current or proposed methods and procedures" and input to "documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because collection design includes choosing among data sources, assessing feasibility of new or modified statistical programs, and ensuring that collection and capture functions integrate properly with downstream systems. That requires capability to review impacts of modified programs and processing specifications and to translate user and subject-matter requirements into system development needs. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills part of this need because the role "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs." It also has "knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs" and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." Those elements are directly relevant to designing collection approaches that are automated and integrated.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because designing collection strategy begins with assessing current and future data requirements, identifying suitable sources, and recommending better methods for retrieving data, especially where passive or already-available sources should be prioritized over direct collection. That requires capability in data requirements assessment, source identification, and recommending retrieval enhancements. The Junior Evaluation Officer is relevant because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," and "identifies and recommends to the Evaluation Manager the usefulness and accessible sources of data to be used in studies." It also "recommends... enhancements to methods for retrieving data," which aligns with the phase's emphasis on selecting the most appropriate collection methods and preferring already-available sources before surveys.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Design frame and sample
description: This sub-process, which applies to all statistical processes involving sampling, is built around digital automation, flexibility, and data quality by design. Whenever frames or registers from administrative, alternative, or partner-held sources are used, partners are expected and supported to apply AI-driven data cleaning and quality control processes prior to data ingestion by Statistics Canada—improving coverage, comparability, and downstream analytic value. The specification of the population of interest, development of the sampling frame, and establishment of sampling criteria and methodology are designed for full integration with end-to-end digital pipelines, supporting automated and seamless flow between pre-collection and post-collection business processes, drastically reducing manual involvement and risk of programmatic 'patches.' Sampling designs must explicitly allow for a range of dynamic and flexible options (including person-based and adaptive sampling), with supporting digital tools enabling real-time optimization informed by diverse data realities and program goals. This ensures the most efficient, quality-driven, and responsive sampling methodologies possible.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires specifying the population of interest, developing the sampling frame, establishing sampling criteria and methodology, and ensuring data quality by design within automated digital pipelines. That creates a need for roles that understand statistical sampling, data acquisition and cleansing, data quality assessment, and translation of subject-matter requirements into operational specifications. The Junior Data Analyst directly fits this need because the work description explicitly includes 'data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing' and 'ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' It also states knowledge of 'survey methodologies, data risk assessment' and 'statistical sampling,' which are central to frame construction and sample design, especially where administrative or partner-held sources must be cleaned and validated before use.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because designing a frame and sample must be integrated with collection and processing operations, with automated flows and reduced manual intervention. That creates a need for roles that can evaluate collection methods, understand data flows and system requirements, and assess impacts of changes to data sources on integrity and completeness. The Operations Officer fills this need because the work description includes 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' and has knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows.' It also explicitly 'analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results,' which is directly relevant when building and maintaining sampling frames from evolving administrative or partner-held sources.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because frame and sample design depends on statistical methodology, the survey universe, and assessing how concepts, definitions, and collection conditions affect results. That creates a need for roles with knowledge of data gathering, estimation, methodological feasibility, and the survey universe so that sampling criteria and methodology are appropriate and adaptable. Economist/Sociologist 2 fits this need because the work description cites 'knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles ... and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation,' as well as 'knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey is required in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques.' It also includes 'knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs,' which supports the design of flexible and responsive sampling methodologies.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the design of frames and samples in digital pipelines requires clear metadata and documented specifications so that population definitions, frame sources, sampling criteria, and methodological choices are consistently implemented across systems. That creates a need for roles that translate requirements into metadata specifications and evaluate metadata quality. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the work description states that the role 'liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' It also includes 'knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data' and 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations,' which are directly relevant to documenting and operationalizing frame and sample design in automated systems.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because designing frames and samples from administrative, alternative, or partner-held sources requires assessing source data validity, consistency, reliability, and the effects of methodological or system changes on downstream outputs. That creates a need for roles that review data quality and examine how revised processing specifications affect integration with other systems. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is implicated because the work description includes 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' It also 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' which supports quality-driven frame development and sample design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Design processing and analysis
description: This sub-process designs the statistical methodology to be applied during the Process and Analyse phases, with a core emphasis on standards-based automation, AI enablement, and digital interoperability. Specifications for routines and rules covering coding, editing, imputation, validation, and data integration/estimation are required to be implemented, where practical, using automated frameworks and AI/ML-driven tools—leveraging SDMX models, .STAT processing, and corporate-standard solutions (e.g., Aria/Colectica). Human analysts and methodologists are focused on reviewing and updating analytic methods for non-standard or novel use-cases, with all standardizable and repeatable components digital, automated, and reproducible by default. Statistical disclosure control and quality assurance methods designed here also leverage automation and AI for rapid, secure, and scalable deployment. All methodologies are documented to be compatible with downstream digital workflows and to support auditing, versioning, and continuous improvement.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is explicitly about designing processing and analysis methodology, including specifications for coding, editing, imputation, validation, data integration/estimation, automation, interoperability, and documentation for downstream workflows. That requires roles able to design or assess processing specifications, analyze and improve processing methods, and translate subject-matter requirements into system-ready specifications. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and has "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" for "designing the specifications for testing of applications" and "developing new processing systems." The role also "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems," which is directly aligned with designing processing routines and rules.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires the design and review of analytic and processing methods for the Process and Analyse phases, especially where methods must be updated for non-standard or novel use-cases and where repeatable components should be standardized and reproducible. That requires analytical staff who can assess existing collection, processing, editing and compilation methods and propose methodological changes. Economist/Sociologist 2 directly meets this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." It also includes "knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles ... and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling," and specifically "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it emphasizes standards-based automation, digital interoperability, and documented methodologies compatible with downstream digital workflows. That creates a strong need for metadata specifications, metadata validation, and methods that support standardized processing and documentation. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," and "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." The role also has knowledge of "statistical metadata concepts and frameworks" and of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata," and "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives," which directly supports interoperable, documented, auditable processing design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes designing routines and rules for data preparation activities such as editing, validation, transformation, and analysis, with an expectation that standardizable components be automated and reproducible. That requires practical capability in data preparation, statistical analysis software, standards conformance, and translating requirements into data development specifications. The Junior Data Analyst is directly relevant because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R," and "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role also includes knowledge of the "data science life cycle, including ... cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization" and the ability to "develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development," which aligns with designing automated and reproducible processing and analysis methods.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it covers editing, validation, processing specifications, quality assurance, and the effect of revised processing specifications on downstream outputs and integration. That requires roles that assess validity of processed data, examine revised processing specifications, and evaluate impacts on output products and services. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because the role "edits, validates ... and disseminates data," "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." The role also "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services," which is directly relevant to designing robust processing and analysis methods.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Design production systems and workflows
description: This sub-process determines the workflow from data collection to dissemination, ensuring all production processes are seamlessly integrated, modular, and event-driven, with automation and AI/ML supporting orchestration, monitoring, and transitions. Workflows are designed to minimize manual intervention and maximize real-time coordination, leveraging digital platforms and automation for every routine or standardized task. The emphasis is on building touchless, continuous data pipelines that allow for automated validation, routing, escalation, and exception reporting. Existing automated solutions and system components are reused wherever possible; if new components are needed, they are built automation- and integration-ready from inception. Staff responsibilities focus on system oversight, addressing exceptions and inefficiencies, and iteratively improving and upgrading automated workflows for future resilience and scalability.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires designing end-to-end workflows from collection through dissemination, with integrated production processes, automation, monitoring, routing, validation, and reuse of system components. That requires roles able to work across collection and processing operations, assess system requirements, understand data flows, and recommend operational alternatives for efficient automated production. The Operations Officer directly fits this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and has knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" as well as responsibility to "assess[] and review[] system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it covers workflow design across the full production chain and stresses integration and coordination of data capture, processing, and dissemination functions. That requires roles that can examine operational system concepts, assess effects of revised processing specifications, and help translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and specifically "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because designing production systems and workflows requires defining how data will be extracted, cleansed, transformed, validated, and managed in continuous pipelines with minimal manual intervention. That requires practical capability in data preparation stages that underpin automated workflows and validation steps. The Junior Data Analyst is directly relevant because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and its knowledge explicitly covers the data life cycle including "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing" and data stewardship to "assess the quality of data, protect and secure data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because workflow design must ensure that production processes remain coherent when procedures, methods, and systems change, and that integrated workflows remain relevant and efficient. That requires roles able to analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation, and presentation methods and propose alternative systems or procedural changes. Economist/Sociologist 2 fits this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and in research and analysis "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems" and "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the workflow extends to dissemination and depends on metadata being correctly produced, stored, validated, and disseminated through integrated systems and reusable components. That requires roles that can translate requirements into specifications for metadata production workflows, test new procedures and systems, and analyze impacts of modified methods and systems. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," and "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Build
description: This phase builds and tests the production solution to the point where it is ready for use in the 'live' environment, leveraging modular automation and AI-driven assembly at every step. The outputs of the Design phase are assembled and configured using digital orchestration pipelines that prioritize reusability, traceability, and compliance with business architecture and security requirements. Automated configuration, integration, and self-testing are employed wherever possible, enabling rapid, reliable, and consistent system deployment. Human expertise is reserved for overseeing automated processes, handling exceptions that cannot be resolved by automation, and driving continuous improvement in modular service creation. New services are developed only to fill gaps, and are built from inception for automation compatibility, modularity, and compliance. The Build phase is structured into seven sub-processes (Figure 9), supporting iteration and parallelization, and is tightly integrated with Design to ensure seamless translation of specifications into robust operational environments.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Build phase is implicating because it focuses on assembling, configuring, integrating and testing production solutions so they are ready for live use, with emphasis on automation, traceability, compliance, and translating design specifications into operational systems. This requires roles that can participate in implementation of automated operations, assess system requirements, support testing, and ensure processing systems work reliably and securely. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows," and "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems." The role also supports testing and operational readiness through "designing the specifications for testing of applications" and maintaining compliance with the Statistics and Privacy Acts.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Build phase is implicating because production solutions are assembled from design outputs and must be configured, integrated, and tested in ways that preserve subject-matter requirements while enabling robust operational deployment. This requires a role that can translate requirements into system specifications, analyze effects of procedural and technology changes, and propose alternative methods where current approaches are not adequate. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because it "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services." The role also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which aligns with build-time integration and refinement.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Build phase is implicating because it includes configuring and testing production and dissemination-related solutions, ensuring that revised processing specifications integrate correctly with existing divisional systems and that outputs remain reliable. This requires a role able to review impacts of new or modified systems, translate requirements into specifications, and assess integration effects on downstream data functions. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because it "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." Those duties directly support build, integration, and readiness activities.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Build phase is implicating because metadata components must also be assembled, validated, loaded into repositories, and tested as part of a compliant and traceable production solution. This requires capability to interpret requirements, participate in testing of new procedures and systems, analyze impacts of changed methods, and ensure metadata production processes remain aligned with policies and security requirements. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," and "interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata." It also has knowledge of "software used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata" and of policies and confidentiality requirements, which supports compliant build activities.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Build phase is implicating because automated configuration, integration, self-testing, and exception handling depend on data preparation, validation, transformation, and support to project teams building operational data solutions. This requires a role with hands-on capability in data extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, standards conformance, and translating requirements into specifications for data development. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and "participates in project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis." It also "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development," which directly supports build implementation and testing.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Reuse or build collection instruments
description: This sub-process describes the activities to build and reuse the collection instruments needed during the Collect phase. Subject matter sponsors are solely responsible for specifying and certifying collection instrument requirements. The actual rendering or building of the instrument is performed by a single accountable centre, which leverages AI and automation to produce survey instruments or extraction routines rapidly and at scale. Automated instrument building enables the strict enforcement of timeliness standards (such as a maximum allowed period between specification and instrument launch), with policies and procedures reformed to reflect these new practices. Direct connection of collection instruments to metadata systems is required to ensure seamless data and metadata capture at source. Staff roles and responsibilities are clearly delineated, removing ambiguity and supporting the rapid, standardized, and high-quality development of instruments for all relevant data acquisition needs.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on building or reusing collection instruments, translating requirements into operational specifications, and ensuring instruments connect directly to metadata systems for standardized, high-quality data capture. This requires capability in collection operations, instrument-related procedures, testing/specification work, and support for operational documentation and training. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and has "knowledge of systems analysis and design... for designing the specifications for testing of applications." The role also supports rollout through "survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures" and by meeting with "subject matter and systems specialists... to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires a "direct connection of collection instruments to metadata systems" and depends on translating requirements into metadata specifications so that data and metadata are captured seamlessly at source. This requires capability in statistical metadata production, validation, standards, procedures, and interpreting client requirements into specifications. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," and "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." The role is also directly aligned with method and system adaptation, as it "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures" and "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because subject matter sponsors must specify and certify collection instrument requirements, and those requirements must be translated into specifications for instrument development under clear roles and timelines. This requires subject-matter capability to define concepts, methods, and procedural needs for collection instruments and to communicate them to system or operational builders. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates." The role also supports refinement of collection approaches through participation in feedback on "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures" and by analyzing "current collection... methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because building automated survey instruments or extraction routines requires translating subject-matter requirements into technical specifications for data capture and acquisition, while ensuring conformity to standards and data quality. This requires capability in data life-cycle knowledge, data capture/acquisition, and liaison with operations and subject-matter specialists to elaborate development conditions. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role includes knowledge of "data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction," and conducts "data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role also directly supports specification work, as it "discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists" and "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because collection instrument development requires liaison among specialists and users to translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications, especially where new or modified statistical programs and processing specifications affect data capture functions. This requires capability in interpreting requirements, assessing impacts of revised processing specifications, and supporting manuals or training tied to new instruments. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is relevant because the role "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs." It also examines "new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems," which is directly pertinent when collection instruments are built or reused within standardized production environments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
description: This sub-process describes the activities to reuse existing components or build new, automation-ready components needed for the Process and Analyse phases. All components—whether dashboard modules, transformation functions, geospatial and information services, or workflow management tools—must be designed for modularity, AI/ML-driven orchestration, and seamless integration into digital, event-driven workflows. Automated self-testing, monitoring, and dynamic integration APIs are core features, enabling real-time responsiveness and automated exchange of data and instructions. Human roles focus on oversight, quality assurance, exception management, and iterative modernization of core analytic assets. The process ensures that the full analytics and processing stack evolves toward touchless, scalable, and intelligent operational pipelines.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is about reusing or building automation-ready processing and analysis components for the Process and Analyse phases, including transformation functions, workflow tools, integration into digital workflows, and quality-assured modernization of analytic assets. That requires capability to prepare, transform, validate, and process data using analytical software, and to help translate requirements into specifications for data development. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization". The role also "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development," which aligns with building reusable components.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automation-ready processing components must support collection/coding/processing operations, be maintainable in automated environments, and include testing, monitoring, and operational integration. That requires operational knowledge of statistical processing systems, system requirements, and the design or modification of operational processes. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems." The role also has "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" for "designing the specifications for testing of applications," which directly supports reusable and self-tested processing components.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because reusable or newly built processing and analysis components must be aligned with subject-matter analytical requirements, integrated into computerized environments, and iteratively improved as methods and technologies change. That requires the ability to translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications and assess processing and analytical methods. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and has knowledge of "statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment." The role also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which matches modernization and reuse/build decisions for analytic components.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because processing and analysis components must integrate with downstream data products, support revised processing specifications, and maintain quality and coordination across systems. That requires capability to assess effects of new or revised processing specifications and adapt outputs and data structures. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems." The role also "adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats," which supports reusable modular components and integration into evolving workflows.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automation-ready processing and analysis components depend on well-structured metadata, documented standards, testing of new procedures and systems, and integration support so that components can operate modularly and reliably in digital workflows. That requires metadata production expertise, requirements translation, and participation in testing and evaluation of methods and systems. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," and "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." The role also "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives," which supports iterative modernization and integration of processing/analysis components.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Reuse or build dissemination components
description: This sub-process describes the activities to build new or reuse existing automation-ready dissemination components needed for the release of statistical products as designated in sub-process 2.1. Dissemination modules—spanning web services, open data, geospatial outputs, microdata access, and even traditional products—are built or upgraded for modularity, machine-actionability, and AI/automation-enabled production. Dynamic output generation, versioning, metadata enrichment, and seamless integration with downstream APIs are all standard, with automation ensuring real-time release, update, and consistency of all published outputs. Human staff are responsible for policy oversight, exception handling, and refinement of complex or user-specific dissemination features that automation cannot yet address.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is specifically about building or reusing dissemination components for releasing statistical products, including automated dissemination, dynamic output generation, metadata enrichment, and integration of outputs into publishable forms. That requires staff who can directly produce, validate, adapt, and disseminate statistical outputs, interpret user dissemination needs, and assess impacts of system or format changes on released products. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role explicitly 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' and 'participates on data production and dissemination teams.' The role also supports automation-ready and evolving dissemination components through analysis of 'changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and by adapting 'data to new definitions or presentation formats.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination components are expected to include 'metadata enrichment,' versioning, and machine-actionable publication, which creates a direct need for roles that prepare, validate, store, and disseminate statistical metadata and help translate dissemination requirements into specifications. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need directly because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.' It also 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems.' This is especially relevant to modular, automation-ready dissemination components and downstream integration because the role has knowledge of 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata' and 'software used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because building or reusing dissemination components requires preparation of outputs, tables, charts, graphs, explanatory text, and operational specifications that support publication products and automated release workflows. That creates a need for staff who can prepare publication-ready statistical outputs and understand operational systems and data flows affecting production and release. The Operations Officer is implicated because the role 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications' and 'prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.' The role also brings relevant systems capability through knowledge 'for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals,' which supports reuse/build decisions for dissemination components.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination components must support publication purposes, presentation methods, and changes in output products and services, including refinement of complex or user-specific dissemination features. That requires subject-matter staff who can help translate requirements into system specifications and assess how procedural or technological changes affect outputs and presentation. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills that need because the role 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes' and 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development.' The role is also relevant because it 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automation-ready dissemination components depend on transformed, validated, standardized data and often require dashboards, visualizations, and other structured outputs suitable for downstream consumption. That creates a need for staff who can prepare data, ensure conformity to standards, and support reporting and visualization products used in dissemination. The Junior Data Analyst is implicated because the role 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' The role also has knowledge of the data science life cycle including 'summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence' and can 'develop briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data,' which supports dynamic output generation and machine-actionable dissemination products.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Configure workflows
description: This sub-process configures the workflows, systems, and transformations used within all business processes—from data collection through to dissemination—to form modular, automation-ready data pipelines. Workflows are assembled, customized, and deployed using digital workflow or business process management platforms, with extensive AI/automation support for orchestration, process monitoring, and autonomous task triggering. These workflows enable seamless, hands-free movement of data and outputs between business process stages, allowing real-time responsiveness and minimizing the need for manual intervention. Human involvement is limited to oversight, rapid workflow adaptation where unique business needs arise, and exception escalation that cannot be managed automatically.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is about configuring end-to-end workflows, systems, and transformations across collection, processing, and dissemination into automation-ready pipelines. That requires roles able to implement and maintain manual and automated operations, understand data flows and processing systems, assess system requirements, and recommend operational alternatives. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has "knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows," and "assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because workflow configuration requires translating business and subject-matter requirements into system specifications, and analyzing current methods to redesign or automate process steps across the statistical production chain. That requires a role that can connect subject-matter needs to system development and evaluate collection-to-presentation procedures. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills that need because it "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because configuring workflows includes setting up downstream production and dissemination processes so data and outputs move seamlessly between stages. That requires a role that can interpret requirements into system specifications, assess revised processing specifications, and understand integration of capture and processing functions with other systems. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because it "liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automation-ready pipelines depend on configured data preparation and transformation steps such as extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, and quality checks. That requires a role with hands-on capability in the data life cycle and in translating requirements into specifications for data development. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation," has knowledge of "data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing," and "liaise[s] with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because workflow configuration also covers metadata-related workflows and systems that support automated production, storage, dissemination, and evaluation across business processes. That requires a role able to interpret requirements into specifications, test new procedures and systems, and analyze impacts of changes in methods and systems. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because it "liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," and "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Test production systems
description: This sub-process is focused on testing the assembled and configured services and workflows by employing automated, AI-powered continuous testing practices. All new programs, routines, and workflow interactions are subject to automated regression and functional tests, with self-testing and monitoring embedded in all integrated components. Testing of data flows, file structure, metadata, and secure transmission is handled primarily by automated pipelines, with full audit trails and auto-generated reports to support later analysis or compliance. Human involvement is reserved for critical sign-off, investigating failed or ambiguous automated tests, managing complex escalations, and verifying regulatory or policy compliance. This approach enables faster, more reliable go-live decisions, reduces operational risk, and assures resilient deployment of production solutions.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires testing of production systems, including automated regression and functional tests, testing of workflow interactions, and validation of data flows and integrated components before go-live. That creates a need for roles that can specify, assess, and support testing of applications and operational processing systems. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the work-description explicitly includes participation in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data', and, more specifically, knowledge 'for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases'. The role also 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems,' which aligns directly with production-system testing and escalation support.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it specifically names testing of 'metadata' and requires automated validation of integrated production components, with auditability and compliance considerations. That creates a need for a role that understands metadata systems, metadata quality, and participation in testing new procedures and systems. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the work-description states that the role 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems.' It also includes 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata' and knowledge of 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata' as well as awareness of 'security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because production-system testing includes validating data flows, file structures, outputs from new or modified systems, and investigating failed or ambiguous automated tests. That creates a need for roles that review data quality impacts from changed systems and assess whether outputs remain valid and reliable. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' The work-description also states that the role 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems,' which directly matches testing integrated workflows and production readiness.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because testing production systems requires checking data preparation, validation, conformity to standards, and data integrity across automated pipelines and workflows. That creates a need for a role capable of validating data and assessing risks to integrity when systems are exercised under test conditions. The Junior Data Analyst is directly relevant because the role 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' The work-description also notes knowledge of 'data risk assessment' and the ability to 'assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity,' which supports investigation of failed tests and validation of production data flows.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because testing assembled and configured production workflows requires assessing how changes in procedures, methods, and computer technology affect outputs and whether alternative systems or procedures are needed before deployment. That creates a need for subject-matter roles that analyze impacts of changed processing methods and system development specifications. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills that need because the role 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development' and 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' The role also 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems,' which is directly relevant to evaluating production-system test results.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Test statistical business process
description: This sub-process manages a field test or pilot of the statistical business process using automated orchestration and AI-driven monitoring to execute, track, and analyze pilot runs. All pilot phases—from collection instrument validation through end-to-end process testing—are tracked through digital platforms that automate data collection, process monitoring, and initial results analysis. Iterative feedback, result synthesis, and suggested improvements are generated by automated and AI-supported systems, enabling automatic identification of issues, process optimization, and faster cycling between iterations. Human experts supervise the piloting phase, make decisions regarding significant process re-designs, and provide final sign-off for transition to live operational status.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on piloting and end-to-end testing of collection, coding, processing, and operational workflows, with monitoring of results and identification of issues before live production. That requires capability to implement and run collection/processing operations in test mode, evaluate methods and results, document issues, and recommend operational alternatives. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and has knowledge used "for designing the specifications for testing of applications." The role also "analyses reported data and work results" and prepares findings on "problems encountered" and recommends alternatives, which aligns closely with pilot monitoring and iterative improvement.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because pilot testing includes automated execution, tracking, and analysis of pilot runs, plus validation of data flows, cleansing, transformation, validation, and quality checks across the process. That requires hands-on analytical support to prepare test data, assess quality, analyze outputs, and support project teams during iterative testing. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software," conducts "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and participates in project teams to support "data management, research and analysis." The role's knowledge of the data science life cycle, including "data capture and acquisition... cleansing, processing... reporting, visualization" is directly relevant to analyzing pilot runs and identifying issues in the tested process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because testing the statistical business process requires assessing whether new or modified systems and procedures produce valid, reliable outputs during pilot runs, and whether changes affect downstream products and services. That requires a role able to review data quality from modified systems, analyze impacts of procedural or system changes, and support interpretation of test outputs. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services," and "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." Those duties directly support pilot-run assessment and readiness for transition to live operations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because pilot testing spans end-to-end statistical processes and requires analysis of whether collection, processing, editing, compilation, and presentation methods remain relevant, as well as feedback on improvements and possible redesigns. That requires subject-matter analytical capacity to assess impacts of methods and procedures and suggest improvements. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." It also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems" and "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services." This is directly aligned with iterative pilot evaluation and redesign decisions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because piloting includes validation of collection instruments, process documentation, and metadata-supported tracking across the statistical process, and requires testing new procedures and systems while evaluating quality. That requires capability in metadata validation, testing of procedures/systems, and reporting on metadata quality implications. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," and "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management." The role also "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives," which supports iterative improvements identified during pilot testing.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because a pilot or field test requires structured evaluation of results, synthesis of findings, identification of issues, and evidence to support decisions on significant redesigns and final sign-off. That requires evaluation-oriented research, data gathering, analysis, and formulation of conclusions under supervision. The Junior Evaluation Officer fills this need because the role "undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects" including "identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data," "applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions," and "provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions." These activities directly support the evaluation and synthesis dimension of pilot testing before operational launch.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Finalise production systems
description: This sub-process finalises and deploys the assembled and configured processes and services—including all modified and newly-created systems—into production, utilizing automated deployment and orchestration tools to ensure readiness. Digital and AI-powered solutions generate all required documentation (technical manuals, user guides, change logs) automatically, and facilitate user onboarding and training via interactive platforms and digital learning modules. Live deployment is monitored and verified through automated tests and real-time telemetry, with issues escalated for human review only in exception cases. Manual staff activities focus on oversight, compliance validation, and approval of production readiness, ensuring the highest standards of operational efficiency and reliability.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centres on deploying modified and newly created systems into production, verifying readiness, monitoring live operation, and approving production use. That requires operational implementation capability, understanding of statistical processing systems, testing specifications, monitoring procedures, and readiness reporting. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems," has knowledge "for designing the specifications for testing of applications," and "analyses reported data and work results" while writing "survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports." These duties align closely with final deployment, operational verification, documentation, training input, and production oversight.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalising production systems includes ensuring that new or modified computer systems and databases are ready for live use, that outputs remain valid after deployment, and that users are supported through documentation and training. That requires a role able to assess impacts of system changes on data products, review quality from modified systems, and contribute manuals and training materials.
