The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems," and "drafts program information manuals and training packages ... and assists in the delivery of training." This directly supports production readiness validation, post-deployment quality assurance, and onboarding/documentation needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because production finalisation explicitly includes generating required documentation, supporting user onboarding and training, and deploying systems that include modified processes and services. That requires a role that contributes to documentation, procedures manuals, training manuals, testing of new systems, and validation of production content. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need for the metadata component of production systems because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," and "provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata and assists with the delivery of training." The role also has knowledge of policies and compliance requirements, including "security and confidentiality," which supports the compliance validation and readiness oversight described in the phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because final deployment requires translating subject-matter requirements into production-ready system specifications, assessing the effects of procedural and technology changes, and supporting manuals and training for operational use. That requires a role that bridges subject matter and system development while analyzing impacts of changed procedures and technologies. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development," "writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports," and "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services." These responsibilities align with production finalisation, readiness assessment, and deployment support where subject-matter implications of system changes must be validated before approval.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Collect
description: This phase collects or gathers all necessary information (data, metadata, paradata) using digitally orchestrated, automation-enabled, and AI-supported systems. Passive data acquisition—from administrative, digital, and system-byproduct sources—is the default and preferred mode, utilizing APIs, automated feeds, and seamless system integrations wherever possible. Active, respondent-driven collection (e.g., surveys) is only used when passive sources are insufficient and must be minimized and justified. All collection methods are subject to real-time intake, validation, and traceability, with human involvement focused on exception handling, compliance oversight, and critical data quality control. The Collect phase is broken into four sub-processes (Figure 10), which can occur sequentially, in parallel, and iteratively, with automation maximizing efficiency and speed in each iteration.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because it is explicitly about gathering information through collection operations, including passive acquisition, respondent contact where necessary, intake, validation, traceability, and compliance oversight. This requires operational capability to run and maintain collection processes, support both manual and automated collection, verify incoming data, advise users on collection methods, and handle respondent or supplier interactions. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results," and has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." The role also supports exception handling and active collection where needed by "contact[ing] data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities," while applying the Statistics Act and Privacy Act in collection activities.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Collect includes not only data but also metadata and paradata, and requires real-time intake, validation, traceability, and system-enabled collection. This creates a need to prepare, validate, store, and disseminate metadata that supports collection processes and ensures collected information is documented and usable across systems. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," and has knowledge of concepts relevant to "the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data." The role also contributes to quality and compliance needs through "statistical metadata quality evaluations" and awareness of the "Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Collect emphasizes digitally orchestrated acquisition, automated feeds, intake, validation, and data quality control. This requires capability in data capture and acquisition, extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, and assessment of data origin and quality. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role includes "data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The knowledge section also explicitly covers the data life cycle, including "data capture and acquisition" and methods to "assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity," which aligns directly with automated collection intake and validation requirements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because collected information must be validated and assessed for quality as it enters production systems, especially when data come from new or modified automated sources and integrated systems. This requires capability to review validity of incoming data and assess effects of system changes on data capture and processing. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "edits, validates" data and "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases." Its research and analysis responsibilities further support collection-phase intake by "examining operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because Collect requires understanding data sources, collection conditions, and feedback on collection methods and procedures, especially where human oversight is needed for quality control and improvement of collection activities. This creates a need for subject-matter analysis of how data are gathered and for recommending improvements to collection approaches. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and has knowledge of "methods and techniques of data gathering." The role also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which directly supports refinement of collection operations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because active collection remains possible when passive sources are insufficient, and the phase includes gathering information from varied sources with attention to data requirements and acquisition. This requires capability to identify, gather, and acquire information from multiple sources and to communicate with clients during acquisition. The Junior Evaluation Officer fills this need because the role "identif[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," and is "required to communicate with clients in the data acquisition process." The role also "collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources, including interviews," which aligns with the collection phase, particularly where active collection is justified.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Create frame and select sample
description: This sub-process establishes the frame and selects the sample for this iteration of the collection, as specified in sub-process 2.4 (Design frame and sample). Automated and AI/LLM-driven technologies are employed to perform record linkage, deduplication, and harmonization across administrative, alternative, and legacy data sources, ensuring the sampling frame is accurate, comprehensive, and consistent. These tools facilitate quality assurance and enhance sample design, especially when coordinating samples between concurrent or overlapping statistical processes. Human experts review, refine, and sign off on the final sampling frame and sample selection, focusing attention on resolving any exceptions or ambiguities surfaced by automated systems.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires establishing an accurate sampling frame and selecting a sample using record linkage, deduplication, harmonization, and quality assurance across multiple data sources. That creates a need for hands-on data preparation, cleansing, transformation, validation, and assessment of data quality, as well as knowledge of statistical sampling and data lifecycle methods. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and has knowledge of the data science lifecycle including "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling" as well as "statistical sampling."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because creating the frame and selecting the sample depends on operational implementation of collection systems, verification of data reliability and consistency, and assessment of changes to data sources that may affect frame completeness and integrity. That creates a need for expertise in collection and processing operations, data verification, and analysis of source changes and system requirements. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because frame creation and sample selection require subject-matter and methodological review of how collection and processing procedures affect data validity, consistency, and the suitability of methods used for statistical operations. That creates a need for staff who can assess collected and processed data, analyze current methods, and propose suitable changes. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," has "knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey ... in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques," and "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated frame construction and sample selection rely on integrating and validating data from diverse sources, checking consistency and reliability, and assessing the effects of revised processing specifications and system changes. That creates a need for a role that reviews data quality from systems and databases and analyzes data from multiple sources. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and "compiles data from diverse sources" and "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because establishing a frame and selecting a sample requires clear metadata, standards, and documentation so that source integration, harmonization, and quality evaluation are consistent across statistical programs. That creates a need for expertise in statistical metadata concepts, validation, and quality evaluation. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," provides advice on "documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," and has knowledge of "survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data" as well as the ability to "evaluate selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Set up collection
description: This sub-process ensures that all people, processes, and technologies (e.g., apps, APIs, devices) are optimally configured to collect data and metadata, as designed, with a strong focus on automation, metadata compliance, and resource flexibility. Routine use of automation is required for recurring data acquisitions and ingestion partnerships. Minimum metadata standards must be checked and validated for every collection or acquisition, with AI-enabled tools applied to extract structured data from unstructured sources and to verify data source credibility—reducing misinformation and ensuring fitness for application. All setup activities also support a 'one workforce' model: staff are cross-trained for multiple roles and resource pools are dynamically allocated or reallocated in real time, based on AI-driven or demand-responsive input, providing greater efficiency and adaptability. For non-survey as well as survey sources, these principles support readiness, quality, and scalability by default.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is about configuring collection operations, processes, and technologies so data and metadata can be collected as designed, including automation, operational readiness, and training support. That requires capability in implementing and maintaining collection operations, evaluating collection methods and procedures, supporting users on collection practices, and preparing operational and training materials. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives,' 'provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding,' and 'provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.' The role also supports setup of systems and workflows through 'knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows' and by 'assess[ing] and review[ing] system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires that metadata be collected and configured with 'minimum metadata standards' checked and validated for every collection or acquisition, with strong emphasis on metadata compliance and readiness. That requires capability to prepare, validate, store, disseminate, and evaluate metadata, advise clients on metadata standards, and test procedures and systems supporting metadata operations. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository,' 'provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines,' and 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems.' The role also specifically supports metadata compliance through 'knowledge of policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata' and quality checks through 'evaluat[ing] selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because setup of collection includes configuring technologies and data ingestion arrangements so that acquired data are fit for use, validated against standards, and assessed for source credibility and integrity, including automated and AI-enabled acquisition contexts. That requires capability in data capture and acquisition, extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, conformity to standards, and assessment of data origin and integrity. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' The role's knowledge base is also directly aligned with setup for automated acquisition because it includes 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing' and 'knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis... in order to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity.' It also supports external-source credibility checks through 'knowledge and understanding of the governance structures of Statistics Canada’s partnerships in order to assess data provided by other levels of government for validity and integrity.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because collection setup must ensure that collection and processing methods are operationally feasible, integrated with systems, and ready for recurring acquisitions and scalable workflows. That requires capability to analyze operational system concepts, assess effects of revised processing specifications, and support integration of data capture and processing functions. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is directly implicated because the role 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.' This supports the setup need to ensure configured collection arrangements and related systems are workable, coordinated, and quality-assured before active collection proceeds.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because setting up collection requires translating subject-matter and program requirements into operational and system specifications, and reviewing collection methods and procedures for improvement before collection begins. That requires capability to liaise with specialists and users, propose changes to collection methods, and analyze current collection procedures for relevance and alternatives. Economist/Sociologist 2 directly fills this need because the role 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' The role also supports setup review through 'analyz[ing] current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because setup of collection includes identifying and acquiring appropriate data sources, understanding data requirements, and recommending enhancements to data retrieval methods so collection arrangements are fit for purpose. That requires capability in data research, source identification, acquisition support, and discussion of data requirements with clients and stakeholders. The Junior Evaluation Officer is implicated because the role 'provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases,' 'discuss[es] data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues,' and 'identifies and recommends to the Evaluation Manager the usefulness and accessible sources of data to be used in studies.' The role also 'recommends... enhancements to methods for retrieving data,' which aligns with configuring collection approaches and acquisition readiness.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Run collection
description: This sub-process implements data collection via a digital-first, automation-driven model, prioritizing passive, system-based, and administrative data pipelines wherever possible. Recurring external data acquisitions are orchestrated through automated scheduling and digital APIs; AI/ML tools auto-populate and validate metadata repositories and perform information management tagging as soon as data is ingested. For survey or respondent-dependent cases, AI/ML-enabled platforms optimize assignment of contacts and resources in real time—dynamically prioritizing, balancing workloads, and reallocating a single, cross-trained resource pool to improve efficiency and data quality. Manual or active contact methods are only pursued when passive collection is not feasible or complete. Continuous digital monitoring, exception reporting, and process-adjustment mechanisms further support collection quality. Human staff are primarily tasked with exception resolution, oversight, and process improvement based on analytics and feedback.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is the operational execution of collection itself, including automated and manual collection channels, monitoring, exception handling, and adjustment of collection procedures. It therefore needs roles that directly implement and maintain collection operations, evaluate collection methods and results, interact with respondents or data suppliers when passive collection is incomplete, and support operational monitoring and improvement. The Operations Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and "contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities." The role also supports the monitoring and improvement aspects through writing "monitoring procedures and management reports" and analyzing "reported data and work results" to recommend alternatives.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the description explicitly states that "AI/ML tools auto-populate and validate metadata repositories" as data is ingested, so collection execution depends on metadata being prepared, validated, stored, and quality-assessed within operational repositories. It therefore needs capability in statistical metadata production, validation, repository loading, and metadata quality evaluation. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," and has knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata." The role also supports process improvement during collection because it "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures" and "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because a digital-first, automation-driven collection model relies on data ingestion, extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation, and quality assessment as data flows in from APIs, administrative systems, and other sources. It therefore needs analytical support for preparing incoming data, validating it, assessing conformity to standards, and supporting analytics-based oversight and process improvement. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role's knowledge of the data science life cycle, including "data capture and acquisition" and "data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing," aligns directly with automated collection pipelines and the analytics used for monitoring and improvement.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because continuous digital monitoring, exception reporting, and process-adjustment mechanisms require staff who can analyze how collection procedures and system changes affect outputs and recommend improvements to collection methods. It therefore needs subject-matter analytical capability tied specifically to collection, processing, and methodological feedback. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." The role also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which matches the process-adjustment and improvement dimension of run collection.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because collection quality in an automated environment depends on reviewing incoming data from systems and databases, validating it, and identifying impacts of new or modified systems on operational outputs. It therefore needs roles that assess data quality from operational systems and support integration between capture and downstream processing. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and "edits, validates" data. The role also "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems," which is directly relevant to automated collection execution and oversight.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because recurring external acquisitions and respondent-dependent collection cases require gathering data from varied sources, discussing data requirements, and supporting acquisition where data must still be obtained actively or through coordination with stakeholders. It therefore needs some capability in data acquisition and collection support, even if not as the primary operational collection role. The Junior Evaluation Officer is implicated because the role "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases," and communication duties include communicating "with clients in the data acquisition process" and discussing "data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues." While this role is evaluation-oriented rather than core collection operations, it is still directly relevant to the acquisition and gathering aspects present in run collection.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Finalise collection
description: This sub-process includes loading the collected data and metadata into a suitable electronic environment for further processing, powered by AI/ML-driven validation and enrichment routines to ensure all metadata repositories and IM tagging are complete, current, and machine-actionable. Routine automatic checks identify and close metadata gaps, verify data structure and governance needs, and prepare files for downstream processing. Finalization is continuously informed by internal and external research, pilot experiments, innovation forums, and evidence-based best practices—enabling iterative improvement and world-leading quality assurance. The subject matter sponsor holds sole responsibility for certifying and accepting the finalized collection data, while operational staff focus on automation, routine execution, and surfacing improvement ideas and lessons learned. Archiving, versioning, and legal compliance handling are embedded as standard, digital-first procedures, ensuring data and metadata are always audit- and analysis-ready.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires loading collected data and metadata into electronic environments, validating and enriching them, ensuring metadata repositories are complete and current, and preparing assets for downstream processing. That creates a direct need for a role focused on statistical metadata production, validation, repository loading, quality evaluation, and compliance. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.' The role also 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata' and 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations,' which aligns with automated checks, metadata gap closure, and iterative improvement. Its knowledge of 'policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata' and awareness of the 'Statistics and Privacy Acts' also matches the phase's embedded legal compliance and audit-readiness requirements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalising collection requires routine execution of collection-processing operations, verification of data structure, preparation of files for downstream processing, and embedded compliance and governance checks. That creates a need for an operational role that works directly on collection, coding, processing, verification, and operational system requirements. The Operations Officer fills that need because the role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and has knowledge of 'methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.' The role also 'assesses and reviews system requirements' and prepares 'reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems,' which supports loading into suitable environments and preparing files for downstream processing. Its explicit knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act supports the phase's legal compliance handling.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it emphasizes validation, enrichment, data structure checks, governance needs, and readiness for further processing in an electronic environment. That creates a need for a role capable of data preparation, cleansing, transformation, validation, quality assessment, and stewardship of data assets. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' The role also requires knowledge of the data science life cycle including 'data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing' and data stewardship, including 'the ability to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use.' Those duties align closely with finalising collection through automated validation/enrichment and ensuring data are analysis-ready.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because after collection is finalized, the data must be validated, reviewed for quality, and made ready for downstream use in a controlled production environment. That creates a need for a role concerned with editing, validating, assessing data quality from systems and databases, and integrating processing outputs into usable statistical products. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' The role also 'examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems,' which directly supports the phase's requirement to prepare files for downstream processing and ensure readiness in electronic environments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes iterative improvement informed by research, pilot experiments, innovation forums, and best practices, as well as feedback on collection, processing, and editing methods. That creates a need for a role that analyzes existing collection and processing procedures and proposes improvements based on observed impacts and constraints. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' It also 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems' and 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' This directly matches the phase's continuous improvement and quality assurance dimension.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is 'continuously informed by internal and external research, pilot experiments, innovation forums, and evidence-based best practices,' which creates a need for roles that gather evidence, analyze data and methods, and recommend enhancements to retrieval or analytical approaches. The Junior Evaluation Officer fills this need by supporting evidence-based improvement: the role 'undertakes literature and data research,' 'identif[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesi[zes] quantitative and qualitative data,' and 'recommends to the Evaluation Manager, enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses.' While not an operational metadata-processing role, it is directly relevant to the phase's explicit requirement that finalization be informed by research and lessons learned for iterative improvement and quality assurance.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Process
description: This phase describes the processing of input data and their preparation for analysis, using modular, version-controlled, automation- and AI/ML-enabled digital workflows. Every sub-process—integrate, classify, check, clean, and transform input data—is configured for event-driven orchestration, reproducibility, and end-to-end automation wherever feasible, ensuring high speed, quality, and consistency. Routine manipulation, error-checking, cleaning, imputation, and integration are handled by AI-enabled modules, with 50% or more of manual interventions eliminated. All processing operations produce full audit trails and documentation for traceability, enabling rapid adjustment and continuous process improvement. Analysts and staff focus on process oversight, exception handling, and innovation, while ensuring all processed outputs are standardized, metadata-rich, and downstream-ready for analysis and dissemination. The Process phase is broken down into eight sub-processes (Figure 11), which may run sequentially, in parallel, or iteratively, as determined by automated orchestration and analytic requirements.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because it is explicitly about processing input data through integration, classification, checking, cleaning, transformation, automation, and preparation for analysis. This requires hands-on capability in data preparation, validation, quality assessment, and use of analytical software within the data life cycle. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and has knowledge of 'data science and its life cycle, including ... cleansing, processing'.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because processing includes operational execution of coding and processing workflows, verification, consistency checks, and maintenance of manual and automated operations. This requires staff who can run and improve processing operations and verify data against specifications. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and has knowledge of 'methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because processed outputs must be checked, edited, validated, standardized, and made downstream-ready for analysis and dissemination. This requires capability to assess validity of processed data, review outputs from systems and databases, and adapt data from multiple sources. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role 'edits, validates ... data', 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases', and 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because it requires processed outputs to be 'metadata-rich' and fully documented for traceability, reproducibility, and downstream use. This creates a need for preparing, validating, storing, and evaluating statistical metadata associated with processing operations and outputs. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository' and contributes to 'documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase is implicating because processing requires assessment of editing, compilation, and processing methods, along with feedback for improvements to procedures and outputs. This requires analytical staff who can examine processing methods and determine impacts on data validity and results. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Integrate data
description: This sub-process integrates data from one or more sources using automated, modular, and AI/LLM-powered pipelines. Record linkage, deduplication, and harmonization are conducted with machine learning and automation as the core methods, minimizing manual intervention. Integration pipelines are event-driven, version-controlled, and produce full audit trails for traceability and continuous improvement. Human experts intervene only to review targeted anomalies, exceptions, and complex analytic challenges, ensuring the integrated dataset is accurate, comprehensive, and ready for further analysis.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on combining data from multiple sources through automated pipelines, including cleansing, transformation, validation, harmonization, and quality assurance so that an integrated dataset is produced and ready for analysis. That requires capability in data preparation, assessing data quality, working with analytical software, and supporting data management workflows. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role explicitly "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing". The role also "participates in project teams and working groups to support data management," which aligns with modular, automated integration pipelines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because integrating data requires processing data from one or more sources, verifying consistency and reliability, assessing impacts of source changes, and supporting automated operational workflows. That requires operational expertise in data processing systems, verification methods, and understanding data flows and database conversion. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and possesses knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows... for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases". Those duties directly support integration, harmonization, and traceable processing.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because integrated data must be validated, assessed for consistency and reliability across sources, and adapted where different source structures or definitions must be reconciled. That requires expertise in compiling data from diverse sources, evaluating validity of processed data and database contents, and adapting data from multiple sources. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "compiles data from diverse sources," and "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." It also "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems" and "adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats... [with] different sources," which is directly aligned with harmonization and integration.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because data integration depends not only on combining records but also on harmonizing definitions, documenting structures, and preserving traceability through metadata so integrated outputs remain interpretable and auditable. That requires production, validation, and evaluation of statistical metadata and the ability to update metadata when methods or systems change. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," ensures metadata is "correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," and has knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata." The role also "analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems... to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats," which directly supports harmonization, version control, and auditability in integrated pipelines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated integration still requires human review of anomalies, exceptions, and complex analytic challenges, as well as assessment of how processing and storage conditions affect resulting integrated data. That requires analytical capability to assess validity, consistency, and the effects of processing methods on outputs. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," has knowledge of "the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data," and "assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored." This aligns with expert intervention on exceptions and complex integration issues.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Classify and code
description: This sub-process classifies and codes input data using modular, automated, and AI/ML-powered pipelines that leverage SDMX and other international standards. Text descriptions and response data are classified and coded primarily by LLM/AI models, which assign pre-determined statistical, geospatial, or industry codes with minimal manual handling. The workflow is event-driven, digitally logged, subject to automated QA/review, and fully auditable. Manual intervention is reserved for new or ambiguous cases, or as last-resort exception handling with domain-expert validation. This approach maximizes accuracy, speed, traceability, and scalability for coding/classification at all process scales.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is directly implicating because it is explicitly about coding and classification of input data, including automated pipelines, QA/review, and exception handling. It therefore needs operational capability in coding methods, processing workflows, verification, and advice on coding practices. This work-description directly fills that need because it states that the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because AI/ML-powered classification and coding pipelines depend on data preparation, transformation, validation, quality checks, and conformity to standards before and during automated coding. It therefore needs technical support for preparing inputs, validating outputs, and working with data science methods. This work-description fills that need because the role "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and requires knowledge of the data science life cycle including "processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization" and "text mining," all of which are directly relevant to automated and AI-assisted classification workflows.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because classification and coding pipelines rely on standards-based structures, documented code meanings, and auditable metadata to support traceability, interoperability, and automated processing using standards such as SDMX. It therefore needs capability to prepare, validate, store, and evaluate metadata and to support standards-based implementation. This work-description fills that need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," has knowledge of "statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally," and understands "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata," which supports the standards and auditability requirements of automated coding/classification.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated classification and coding still require review of processed outputs, assessment of validity and consistency, and support for downstream use of coded data. It therefore needs capability to assess processed data quality and effects of revised processing specifications. This work-description fills that need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and in research and analysis "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness" and "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because manual intervention is reserved for ambiguous or new cases and requires domain-expert validation of concepts, definitions, and classifications. It therefore needs subject-matter analytical capability to assess whether coding outputs are valid under the concepts and conditions of the statistical program. This work-description fills that need because the role participates in analysis and "suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and has knowledge of "the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data" as well as the ability to analyze "current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Review and validate
description: This sub-process examines and validates data using modular, automated digital tools and AI/LLM-enabled validation routines. ML and LLMs flag missing data, inconsistencies, outliers, and errors, routing only ambiguous, complex, or systemic anomalies to human experts for further investigation and correction. All validation is digitally orchestrated with complete audit logging, reproducibility, and ongoing version control. This approach ensures rapid, scalable, and transparent validation with minimal manual intervention, allowing for continuous adjustment and quality improvement.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is explicitly about examining and validating data, detecting missing data, inconsistencies, outliers and errors, and escalating ambiguous anomalies for human investigation and correction. That requires capability in data validation, data cleansing, assessing data quality, and working with analytical tools in a reproducible digital workflow. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and 'supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R'. The role also includes knowledge to 'assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity,' which aligns with investigating anomalies flagged by automated validation routines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because review and validation requires direct responsibility for editing and validating data, assessing whether outputs from systems and databases are reliable, and supporting quality-focused correction and downstream use. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly matches these needs because the role's key activities state it 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.' Its analytical responsibilities further align with validation by stating it 'Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness' and uses 'socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.' This is directly relevant to human review of anomalies surfaced by automated validation tools.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated and human validation both depend on methods to verify data against specifications, ensure reliability and consistency, and investigate irregularities in operational data flows. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives.' Most directly, the knowledge requirements include 'Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.' The role also 'contacts data suppliers or respondents to ... clarify problems or irregularities,' which aligns with resolving ambiguous or systemic anomalies routed from automated validation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because review and validation includes assessing the validity of processed data, examining effects of processing and editing methods, and proposing changes where anomalies or quality issues are found. The Economist/Sociologist 2 is directly relevant because the role 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' It also requires 'Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data' and 'Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' These capabilities support expert investigation of complex or systemic anomalies identified during validation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because validation in a digitally orchestrated environment also requires validating associated statistical metadata, evaluating metadata quality, and ensuring documentation and standards remain consistent for reproducibility, audit logging and version control. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository' and 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations.' The role also has knowledge of 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata' and 'evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs in accordance with pre-defined quality guidelines.' This is directly implicated where validation processes depend on accurate metadata and documented quality controls.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because examining and validating data, especially where anomalies are flagged and interpreted by humans, requires identifying, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data and supporting interpretation of findings. The Junior Evaluation Officer is relevant because the role 'identif[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data' and 'provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions.' It also 'applies analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results' and 'collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources' while applying 'established methods and techniques used for sorting, summarizing, analyzing and interpreting data.' These capabilities support human review of ambiguous or complex anomalies, even though the role is less directly centered on operational statistical validation than the data-focused roles above.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Edit and impute
description: Where data are considered incorrect, missing, unreliable, outdated, or duplicated, edits and imputations are made through automated, modular, and AI/LLM-powered digital pipelines. LLMs and ML modules suggest and apply replacements or corrections as standard, tracking all actions and metadata in a comprehensive audit trail. Human analysts intervene only for novel, complex, or systemic data problems, and for reviewing and signing off automated edits where required. This ensures fast, accurate, and transparent correction of data with minimal manual processing.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is specifically about correcting problematic data through editing, imputation, validation, and review of automated processing results. It therefore needs roles that directly perform or assess data editing and validation, review data quality from systems, and work with processing methods and specifications. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fits this need because the role explicitly "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data" and "Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases." The role also supports the analytical side of edit-and-impute through "Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness" and by examining "new or revised processing specifications" to determine effects on processing functions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because edit and impute requires operational processing capability to verify data, handle irregularities, and maintain reliable automated and manual processing workflows when data are incorrect, missing, unreliable, outdated, or duplicated. It therefore needs roles involved in collection/coding/processing operations, verification, and assessment of processing system requirements. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," and has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." The role also "Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives" and "Assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems," which is directly relevant to automated edit-and-impute pipelines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because edit and impute depends on data cleansing, transformation, validation, and quality assessment, especially where automated pipelines and AI/ML modules are used and human analysts review complex cases. It therefore needs roles with hands-on data preparation and data quality capabilities using analytical software. The Junior Data Analyst directly matches this because the role "Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role also requires knowledge of the data science life cycle including "cleansing, processing" and knowledge of methods to "assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity," which aligns closely with edit-and-impute activities.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because edit and impute includes not only correcting data but also handling metadata and auditability: the phase description explicitly says automated pipelines are "tracking all actions and metadata in a comprehensive audit trail." It therefore needs roles that prepare, edit, validate, and evaluate statistical metadata so that edits, imputations, and their provenance are properly documented. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because the role "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository." The role also contributes to methods for "producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata" and has knowledge relevant to "collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data" as well as "statistical metadata quality evaluations," all of which support the metadata and audit-trail dimension of edit and impute.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because edit and impute requires subject-matter review of processed data, assessment of validity of collected and processed data, and feedback on editing methods and procedures, especially when human analysts must intervene for novel, complex, or systemic problems. It therefore needs roles that analyze data and propose improvements to editing and processing methods. Economist/Sociologist 2 fits this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." The role also has knowledge "to assess the validity of collected and processed data" and explicitly "Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Derive new variables and units
description: This sub-process derives data for variables and units needed to deliver required outputs using modular, automation- and AI-powered methods. Digital pipelines apply arithmetic and formula-based logic, iterating as needed and recording all derivations and transformations with a traceable audit trail. Manual intervention is reserved for rare, non-standard or complex derivations beyond automation, with staff focusing on validation and insight for exceptions. This structure maximizes efficiency, reproducibility, and transparency in all variable/unit derivation steps.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on deriving new variables and units through automated and formula-based transformations, with strong needs for data transformation, processing, validation, and reproducible handling of derived outputs. It therefore requires roles that can execute data transformation steps, use analytical software, assess data quality, and support exception handling when derivations are complex. The Junior Data Analyst directly fits this need because the role explicitly "conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin" and supports projects using quantitative analysis software such as "Python, SAS, STATA, R". The work description also states knowledge of the data science life cycle including "processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization" and the ability to "derive meaningful information from data," which directly aligns with deriving new variables and units.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because deriving new variables and units depends on processing logic, verification against specifications, and maintaining reliable outputs when transformations are applied in production systems. It therefore needs operational capability in data processing, verification, and assessment of system requirements and impacts on outputs. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data" and has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." The role also "assesses and reviews system requirements" and "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results," which is directly relevant to automated derivation pipelines and traceable transformations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because deriving new variables and units is not only a transformation task but also requires assessing whether derived outputs are valid, consistent, and analytically meaningful, especially where manual intervention is needed for exceptions. It therefore needs subject-matter analytical capacity to evaluate processed data and the effects of methods and procedures on outputs. The Economist/Sociologist 2 is directly relevant because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures" and has knowledge of "the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data." The role also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which supports validation and refinement of derivation methods.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because derived variables and units must be validated and assessed for consistency, reliability, and appropriateness before they can support required outputs. It therefore needs roles that work directly with edited and validated data products and can assess impacts of revised processing specifications and alternative manipulations. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because the role "edits, validates" data and "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases." Its analytical responsibilities include "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness" and "adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats," which closely matches the derivation of new variables and units from existing data structures.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because derivation steps in automated pipelines must be documented and traceable, with all derivations and transformations recorded in an audit trail. It therefore needs support for the metadata that describes derived variables, transformations, standards, and quality implications. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer is relevant because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository" and has knowledge of concepts and procedures relating to "the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata." The role also "analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats," which directly supports documenting derived variables and maintaining traceability of transformations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Calculate weights
description: This sub-process creates weights for unit data records through modular, event-driven automated algorithms, according to methodologies determined in phase 2.5. All steps and formulae, including adjustments for non-response or benchmarking, are handled digitally and recorded in procedural audit logs. Staff intervene when innovative methods, unexpected results, or diagnostic reviews are needed; otherwise, the process runs hands-free, ensuring speed, precision, and traceability in weight calculation.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires automated statistical processing of unit records, application of established weighting methodologies, and staff review when diagnostics reveal unexpected results. That creates a need for roles that can work with quantitative statistical methods, prepare and validate data, assess data quality, and support modeling or analytical processing in software-driven environments. The Junior Data Analyst fits this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R" and "conducts data preparation techniques" including "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality." The knowledge section also directly supports weighting work through "knowledge of the theories, principles, practices, and methodologies of statistics and mathematics in order to conduct the requisite modelling" and knowledge of "processing" and "modeling" across the data science life cycle.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because weight calculation is part of statistical processing and depends on reliable automated operations, verification to specifications, and review of processing results when anomalies or unexpected outputs occur. That creates a need for operational roles involved in automated data processing, evaluation of methods and results, and analysis of impacts on program outputs. The Operations Officer fills that need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications."
