The role also "analyses reported data and work results" and prepares findings on how operations were conducted, which aligns with intervention for diagnostic reviews and unexpected results.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because calculating weights requires statistical estimation-oriented processing, assessment of methodological effects on outputs, and analytical review when innovative methods or unexpected results arise. That creates a need for roles with knowledge of statistical estimation, validity assessment of processed data, and analysis of processing methods and methodological changes. Economist/Sociologist 2 fits this need because the role includes "knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling." It also includes "knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data" and the ability to "analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which is directly relevant when weighting diagnostics require staff intervention.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated weight calculation produces processed statistical outputs that must be checked for consistency, reliability, and appropriateness, especially when adjustments such as non-response or benchmarking are applied and when unexpected results require review. That creates a need for roles that assess processed data quality and examine effects of revised processing specifications. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and in research and analysis "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." The role also "examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions," which supports review of automated weighting procedures and outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Calculate aggregates
description: This sub-process creates aggregate data and population totals using modular, digital automation pipelines, generating all statistical summaries, weights, and dispersion measures hands-free. Event-driven algorithms apply the full range of aggregations, error calculations, and summary statistic logic, recording all processes in comprehensive audit logs for traceability and QA. Human expert action is required only for advanced analytic extensions or for reviewing flagged anomalies or exceptions in automated results.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is specifically about producing aggregate data, population totals, summary statistics, weights, and dispersion measures through automated processing pipelines, with human review focused on anomalies and advanced analytic extensions. That requires capability in quantitative statistical analysis, data processing, summarization, and use of analytical software to support or review automated aggregation outputs. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R" and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting" as well as "theories, principles, practices, and methodologies of statistics and mathematics." Those elements directly support calculation and review of aggregates and summary measures.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because aggregate calculation produces statistical summaries and totals that must be validated for consistency, reliability, and appropriateness, and may require human review of flagged exceptions from automated results. That requires a role able to compile data into tables and outputs, assess validity of processed data, and interpret requests for statistical tabulations. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," and in research and analysis "compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output," while it also "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." These duties align directly with producing and checking aggregate outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because calculating aggregates depends on statistical program data being analyzed, with attention to compilation methods, processing effects, and possible improvements when automated outputs show anomalies or methodological issues. That requires subject-matter analytical capacity tied to statistical estimation, modeling, and assessment of compilation methods. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data," "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and requires "knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles ... and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling." It also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which is directly relevant when reviewing aggregate calculations and exceptions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated aggregate calculation sits within statistical processing operations and depends on reliable processing systems, verification methods, and review of outputs for integrity and completeness. That requires operational expertise in processing data and assessing system requirements and output quality. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results." The role also "assesses and reviews system requirements" for processing systems, which supports the automated pipeline context of aggregate calculation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Finalise data files
description: This sub-process brings together and finalizes the results of all previous sub-processes in the phase, producing data files (micro- or macro-level) in fully standardized, open, and machine-actionable formats by default. All datasets and supporting documentation are versioned, digitally logged, and immediately available for reproducible handoff to subsequent analysis or dissemination phases. Technical staff ensure compliance with standards and continuous skills development, and all processes are supported by automated documentation and audit trails, supporting immediate traceability, interoperability, and readiness for deployment across business domains.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it requires the final assembly, validation and release-readiness of data files in standardized, machine-actionable formats, with traceability and readiness for downstream dissemination or analysis. That creates a need for roles that directly edit, validate, adapt, and disseminate data outputs, and that assess effects of system or methodological changes on final data products. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role explicitly "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," and "Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases." It also supports finalization through research and analysis functions that "Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output," "Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness," and "Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats," which aligns closely with producing finalized, standardized files ready for handoff.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalized data files must be standardized, documented, version-ready, and reproducible, with supporting documentation available for immediate handoff. That creates a need for metadata production, validation, repository loading, documentation maintenance, and quality evaluation of metadata that accompanies finalized datasets. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository." The role also supports standardized and traceable finalization by providing input on "methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata," contributing to "documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals," and analyzing changes to determine "the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats," all of which directly support documented, interoperable, machine-actionable final data files.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalising data files depends on data preparation, cleansing, transformation, validation, conformity to standards, and maintenance of organized work files that support reproducibility and traceability. That creates a need for a role that performs hands-on preparation and quality-oriented consolidation of data assets before handoff. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role also "Organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies" and "Maintains work files," which aligns with the sub-process requirement that datasets and supporting documentation be digitally logged, traceable, and reproducible.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because bringing together and finalizing outputs from prior processing steps requires operational control over processing activities, verification against specifications, and awareness of data flows and database conversion or maintenance affecting final files. That creates a need for a role involved in processing operations and in ensuring reliability and consistency of outputs. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data" and has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." The role also has contextual knowledge of "computer processing and data flows" and "the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals," which is directly relevant to finalizing deployable data files.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because final data files must reflect completed processing, editing, compilation and presentation decisions, and must be assessed for consistency, reliability, and suitability for subsequent use. That creates a need for subject-matter roles that analyze the effects of methods and procedures on outputs and help ensure the validity of finalized data products. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role participates in "the analysis of statistical program data" and in suggesting feedback on "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures." The role also has knowledge "to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents," and conducts analysis of "current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which supports robust finalization of data files.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Analyse
description: In this phase, statistical outputs are produced and examined in detail using automated, AI-powered, and modular analytical pipelines. All workflows—from draft output and commentary preparation to validation and finalization—leverage digital automation and AI/ML-driven solutions, producing real-time, reproducible, and version-controlled results. Automated generation of daily write-ups, dashboards, and other standardized products is the norm, with human analysts focused on interpretation, contextualization, and providing tailored, nuanced analysis for users. Intelligent, real-time validation and anomaly detection are embedded throughout. The phase is fully iterative and feedback-driven, supporting rapid, responsive, and continuous analytic enhancement. The Analyse phase and its sub-processes are applicable to all outputs regardless of data source, and support the seamless transition to dissemination.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because it centers on producing and examining statistical outputs, validating results, generating analytical products such as dashboards and write-ups, and interpreting findings for users. That requires capability in quantitative analysis, data preparation, validation, reporting, visualization, and use of analytical software. The Junior Data Analyst directly fills this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R" and "conducts data preparation techniques" including "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality." The role also supports analytic outputs through "analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools" and has knowledge of "reporting, visualization, business intelligence" and "exploratory/ confirmatory, predictive analysis."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because Analyse requires statistical outputs to be produced, examined for consistency and reliability, interpreted, and prepared for transition to dissemination. That requires a role able to compile outputs, assess data quality, summarize meaning, and respond to user-oriented output needs. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," and in research and analysis "compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output," "summarizes and describes meaning of data," and "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." The role also "drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data," which aligns with commentary preparation and analytical interpretation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because Analyse emphasizes analysis of statistical program data, identification of trends, interpretation, feedback on upstream methods, and preparation of analytical material for publication and internal use. That requires subject-matter analytical capability tied to statistical outputs and their interpretation. The Economist/Sociologist 2 directly fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes," "identifies statistical trends and developments," and "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures." The role also has knowledge to "identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series" and to assess "the validity of collected and processed data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because Analyse includes embedded validation, anomaly detection, examination of outputs, and iterative feedback to improve methods and outputs. That requires operational knowledge of data processing results, verification practices, and analysis of output integrity. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," and has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." The role also "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results" and "analyses reported data and work results" to recommend alternatives, which supports iterative analytic enhancement.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because Analyse includes preparation of outputs, commentary, interpretation of quantitative and qualitative evidence, and formulation of conclusions for reporting. That requires analytical synthesis and support for reports and briefings. The Junior Evaluation Officer is relevant because the role "identif[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," "appl[ies] analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulat[es] conclusions," and "provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions." The role also "provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda," which aligns with analytical write-ups and commentary preparation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because reproducible, version-controlled analytical outputs and seamless transition to dissemination depend on accurate metadata and metadata quality evaluation to support interpretation, standardization, and output usability. That requires preparation, validation, and evaluation of statistical metadata associated with outputs. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations," and contributes to reports describing "the results of metadata quality evaluations." The role also has knowledge of "survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data" and evaluates metadata quality indicators, supporting the analytical phase's need for documented, reliable, and dissemination-ready outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Prepare draft outputs
description: This sub-process transforms processed and finalized data into statistical outputs using automated, AI-powered pipelines. Outputs—including indices, seasonally adjusted statistics, mapped data, geo-statistical services, write-ups, dashboards, and methodological documentation—are generated by default through LLM/AI-driven automation. Human analysts intervene to interpret, refine, or tailor outputs for specialized, complex, or critical communication needs. AI-generated methodological notes and narratives accompany all outputs, documenting analytic approaches and logic. This automation-first approach maximizes efficiency, consistency, and allows analysts to focus on providing added value and insight.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is about turning finalized data into publishable statistical outputs, including tables, dashboards, write-ups and methodological documentation, while also requiring human intervention to interpret and refine outputs for specialized communication needs. That requires capability to compile data into outputs, assess and summarize meaning, adapt presentation formats, and draft explanatory material for publication. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role explicitly 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data', 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations', and in research and analysis 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output', 'summarizes and describes meaning of data', and 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats'. It also supports narrative output because it 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because draft outputs include analytical write-ups, publication material, and human refinement of automated outputs where interpretation is needed. That requires staff who analyze statistical program data, identify trends, and help prepare analytical material for publication purposes. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills that need because the role 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes', 'identifies statistical trends and developments', and writes technical and subject-matter material, including 'writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology'. Those duties align with interpreting AI-generated outputs and refining them into usable analytical products.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated draft outputs include dashboards, visualizations, reports and other statistical products derived from processed data, and human analysts are needed to refine and communicate those outputs clearly. That requires data analysis capability plus the ability to prepare analytical reports, presentations and dashboards. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role 'supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software', and its knowledge requirements explicitly include 'summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence'. It also states that 'writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools' and that data literacy is needed 'to develop briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because all outputs are accompanied by methodological notes and narratives documenting analytic approaches and logic, so there is a direct need to prepare, validate and disseminate statistical metadata and related documentation. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata', ensures it is loaded to the corporate repository, and 'contributes written information to be used as input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals'. The role also has knowledge of 'survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data', which supports the methodological documentation component of draft outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because preparing draft outputs can include statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text, especially where operational program results are turned into regular or ad-hoc publications. That requires capability to design output products and explain results. The Operations Officer fills that need because the role explicitly 'designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications' and also 'responds orally and in writing ... to provide information on ... the use of program results.' These duties directly support the production and refinement of draft statistical outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because draft outputs include reports, presentations and briefing-style narrative products derived from analyzed data, and human intervention is needed to interpret findings and support communication to management or stakeholders. That requires staff who can synthesize quantitative and qualitative data and provide supporting material for reports and presentations. The Junior Evaluation Officer fills that need because the role 'identif[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data', 'provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions', and 'provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda'. While evaluation-focused, these activities are directly relevant to preparing draft analytical outputs and narratives from finalized data.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Validate outputs
description: This sub-process is where outputs are validated using automated, AI- and ML-powered, real-time digital workflows. Anomaly detection, benchmarking against historical data, metadata and paradata checks, macro editing, and internal/external confrontations are executed with machine-driven QA and pattern recognition. Complex, novel, or ambiguous findings are escalated to human statistics experts for review and contextual analysis, ensuring that outputs are validated rapidly, consistently, and with high assurance of quality.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is explicitly about validating statistical outputs through anomaly detection, benchmarking, metadata checks, macro editing, and escalation of ambiguous findings for expert review. That requires roles able to validate data outputs directly, assess consistency and reliability, review quality impacts from systems and databases, and support dissemination-ready outputs. This work-description directly fits because it states that the role "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data" and "Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases." It also specifies capability to "analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability" and to "analyze and evaluate data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness," which aligns closely with output validation and confrontation against expected patterns.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because output validation depends on checking data quality, conformity to standards, data origin, and detecting anomalies in prepared outputs before release or further use. That requires hands-on analytical capability with data validation workflows and quality assessment methods. This work-description fills that need because it explicitly includes "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." It also notes knowledge of the data science life cycle including "processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization" and knowledge needed "to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity," which is directly relevant to automated and expert-assisted validation of outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it specifically mentions "metadata and paradata checks" as part of output validation. That creates a need for expertise in preparing, editing, validating, evaluating, and reporting on metadata quality so that outputs can be assessed against metadata standards and documentation. This work-description directly satisfies that need because the role "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata" and "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations." It further states knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata" and the ability to "Evaluate selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs in accordance with pre-defined quality guidelines," which is highly specific to the metadata-checking component of output validation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because validating outputs includes verifying reliability and consistency to specifications, confronting irregularities, and reviewing operational results where automated workflows identify issues. That requires operational knowledge of verification methods and the ability to analyze reported data and output changes. This work-description fits because it includes "Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications." It also states that the role "Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives" and "Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results," which supports validation of outputs and investigation of anomalies arising from production processes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because complex, novel, or ambiguous findings are escalated to human statistics experts for contextual analysis, and because validation includes assessing trends, consistency, and the effects of methods and definitions on outputs. That requires subject-matter analytical expertise to interpret unusual findings and judge validity in context. This work-description fills that need because it says the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data," "Identifies statistical trends and developments," and "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures." It also includes knowledge "to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data," which directly supports expert review of escalated validation issues.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Interpret and explain outputs
description: This sub-process interprets and explains outputs using LLM/AI-powered narrative generation, visualization, and automated analytics to provide first-draft explanations and insight. Statisticians and analysts review and refine these drafts, supplementing them with domain expertise, context, and additional analytics as needed to make results accessible and meaningful, especially for nuanced or high-impact topics.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on interpreting statistical outputs, generating explanations, and making results accessible through narrative, visualization, and analytics. That requires capability to analyze data, identify trends and developments, and help prepare analytical material for publication or internal use. This work-description directly fits that need because it states the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes," "identifies statistical trends and developments," and "writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications." It also includes assessing how concepts and collection conditions affect results, which supports nuanced explanation of outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because outputs must be interpreted, explained, and often turned into charts, tables, articles, and client-facing statistical products. That requires a role able to summarize the meaning of data, assess reliability, and draft interpretive material for dissemination. This work-description fills that need because it explicitly says the role "drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used," and in research and analysis it "compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output" and "summarizes and describes meaning of data." Those duties align directly with reviewing AI-generated first drafts and refining explanations for users.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because interpreting and explaining outputs depends on analytical capability, visualization, reporting, and communication of findings to managers and clients. That requires a role with data literacy, analytical reporting, and visualization skills. This work-description fits because it supports studies using statistical analysis software, and its knowledge section includes "summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence" as part of the data science life cycle. It also states that "writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science" and that data literacy includes the ability to "read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data." These are directly relevant to refining AI-assisted narratives and explanations of outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because explanation of outputs, especially nuanced or high-impact results, requires interpretation of data in context and formulation of conclusions that can support reports, presentations, and briefings. That requires a role able to analyze and synthesize quantitative and qualitative data and provide interpretive input. This work-description fills that need because it "appl[ies] analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulat[es] conclusions," "provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions," and "provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda." Those responsibilities align with reviewing and refining first-draft explanations of outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because explaining outputs often requires supporting explanatory text, tables, charts, and communication about program results. That requires a role able to prepare visual/statistical presentation materials and explain results in operational context. This work-description supports that need because it "designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications" and "responds orally and in writing to enquiries ... to provide information on ... the use of program results." Its analysis of changes to outputs and program results also helps ensure explanations are accurate and meaningful.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because outputs must be made accessible and meaningful, and that often depends on accurate metadata and documentation that explain concepts, methods, and quality to users. That requires a role able to prepare, validate, and disseminate metadata and contribute to explanatory documentation and quality reporting. This work-description fills that need because it "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," provides advice on metadata, and "contributes written information to be used as input to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations." It also has knowledge of subject matter concepts relevant to "the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data," which supports explanatory context around outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Apply disclosure control
description: This sub-process applies disclosure control by default using AI-driven, automation-enabled privacy/SCD tools, which automatically assess, suppress, or perturb outputs for confidentiality per established policy. All actions are digitally logged and audited. Outputs only reach human reviewers when the automation detects elevated, ambiguous, or non-standard disclosure risks, ensuring privacy compliance by default and at scale.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on protecting confidentiality in outputs through automated disclosure control, policy-based assessment, and escalation of ambiguous disclosure risks for human review. This requires a role that works directly with the dissemination of statistical outputs and applies legal/policy requirements concerning confidentiality before release. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because the role explicitly "edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," and has "particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance." The role also "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," which aligns with evaluating outputs produced through automated privacy/SCD tools before dissemination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated disclosure control depends on operational processing environments that enforce confidentiality rules, support automated handling of outputs, and maintain compliant practices when data move through collection/coding/processing systems. This requires a role involved in automated operations and knowledgeable about confidentiality obligations in statistical processing. The Operations Officer fills that need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," and has knowledge of "systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows" relevant to operationalizing automated controls. The work description also states that the position must have "particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance," directly supporting disclosure-control application.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because disclosure control automation must assess disclosure risk, protect and secure data, and support responsible use of outputs, especially when elevated or ambiguous risks are detected. This requires analytical capability in data risk assessment, data validation, and secure stewardship of data assets in technology-enabled workflows. The Junior Data Analyst fits this need because the role conducts "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," all of which are relevant to preparing and checking outputs subject to disclosure control. The work description also explicitly includes "data risk assessment" and states that data literacy includes the ability to "protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use," which directly aligns with automated privacy/SCD review.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because disclosure control is applied to statistical outputs during compilation and presentation, and requires human review capacity for cases where automated tools flag non-standard confidentiality risks. This requires a role that works with presentation of statistical data and applies confidentiality legislation and policies in handling outputs. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills that need because the role participates in "collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data," and analyzes methods and procedures affecting outputs. The work description further states that the position must have "particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance," making it directly relevant to disclosure-control review of outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because disclosure control actions are policy-driven, digitally logged, and audited, so metadata and documentation about confidentiality handling, dissemination conditions, and compliance context can be important to support automated and reviewed release processes. This requires a role concerned with producing, validating, and evaluating metadata under relevant policies and with awareness of confidentiality obligations. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," provides advice on "documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines," and participates in "testing of new procedures and systems." The work description also states that the position must have "an awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance," which supports disclosure-control documentation and compliant dissemination context.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Finalise outputs
description: This sub-process finalises and packages outputs using digital, automation-driven tools and workflows, ensuring all required metadata, commentary, technical notes, consistency checks, and documentation are produced and collated automatically to the highest standard. Human experts are responsible for sign-off, review of flagged anomalies, and decision-making on exceptional release scenarios or nuanced dissemination requirements. Routine approval, translation, and pre-release briefing are streamlined by digital platforms, maximizing output quality and deployment speed.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly requires outputs to be finalised and packaged for dissemination, with metadata, commentary, technical notes, consistency checks, and documentation completed to a high standard. That creates a need for a role that directly edits, validates, prepares, and disseminates statistical outputs, while also assessing output quality and adapting outputs to presentation formats. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "Drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used," and "Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output" while "Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness" and "Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats." These duties align closely with final packaging, commentary, consistency checks, and dissemination-ready output preparation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it specifically states that "all required metadata" must be produced and collated automatically as part of finalising outputs. That creates a need for a role focused on preparing, validating, disseminating, and evaluating metadata quality, as well as maintaining related documentation and procedures. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository," "Provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata," and "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management." The role also has knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata," which is directly relevant to the metadata and documentation requirements of finalising outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalising outputs includes producing commentary, technical notes, consistency checks, and handling review of flagged anomalies before release. That creates a need for a role able to analyze statistical program data, prepare analytical material for publication, identify trends, and assess presentation methods and data validity. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes," "Identifies statistical trends and developments," and "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures." It also includes writing "detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms" and analyzing "current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," which supports technical notes, commentary, and expert review of output quality before release.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because final output packaging requires consistency checks, validation of outputs, and review of anomalies arising from automated workflows. That creates a need for a role that can assess data quality, perform validation, and support reporting and presentation materials used in release products. The Junior Data Analyst is relevant because the role "Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin," and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "summarization, reporting, visualization." The role also has writing skills to "draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material," which supports the consistency-checking and packaging aspects of finalising outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because finalising outputs includes consistency checks, explanatory material, and ensuring outputs are reliable and suitable for dissemination. That creates a need for a role that can verify statistical data, prepare tables and explanatory text, and analyze the integrity and completeness of outputs. The Operations Officer fills part of this need because the role "Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications," has knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications," and "Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results." These duties directly support final output checks and packaging for publication.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it includes production of commentary, briefing material, and documentation to support final release and expert sign-off. That creates a need for a role that contributes supporting data and written material for reports, presentations, briefing notes, and memoranda. The Junior Evaluation Officer is relevant to this aspect because the role "Provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management" and "Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions." While not a primary dissemination role, this work-description supports the commentary and briefing components required when outputs are being finalised and prepared for release decisions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Disseminate
description: This phase manages the release of statistical data and their products to users using automation-driven, API-first, and metadata-enriched delivery workflows and platforms. All assembling, cataloguing, metadata enrichment, and release processes are automated and performed in real-time, producing products that are dynamically accessible, searchable, and machine-actionable by both human and AI agents. Outputs are prepared for API-driven consumption, optimized for AI search, and enriched with comprehensive metadata to ensure discovery and reuse across systems. Human staff engage only for policy setting, exception handling, and specialized user support. The Disseminate phase is structured into five sub-processes (Figure 13), which may operate sequentially, in parallel, or iteratively, as best fits the digital dissemination ecosystem.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because it is explicitly about releasing statistical data and products to users through automated, metadata-enriched dissemination workflows, with human involvement focused on policy, exceptions, and specialized user support. That requires capability to disseminate data products, interpret user requests, prepare outputs for users, assess output quality, and provide consultative support. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role explicitly 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations,' 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users,' and 'Participates on data production and dissemination teams.' The role also supports dissemination quality and output preparation through work such as 'Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output' and 'Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because dissemination is described as metadata-enriched, searchable, machine-actionable, and optimized for discovery and reuse across systems. That requires strong capability in preparing, validating, storing, and disseminating statistical metadata, as well as supporting metadata quality and repository loading. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role explicitly 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.' It also supports dissemination-system needs by 'provid[ing] feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata,' assisting with 'statistical metadata quality evaluations,' and participating on teams tasked with the 'production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' These duties align directly with the phase's emphasis on metadata enrichment, discoverability, and reuse.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because dissemination outputs must be dynamically accessible, searchable, and consumable by users and systems, and human staff may still provide specialized user support and prepare publication-oriented analytical material. That requires capability to analyze program data, prepare analytical material for publication, and assist users with statistical data. The Economist/Sociologist 2 helps fill this need because the role 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes' and 'Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.' The role also has knowledge tied to 'presentation of statistical data' and analyzes 'the effect on data output, products and services,' which supports dissemination-oriented outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because dissemination includes assembling outputs, making them accessible to users, and supporting publication products such as tables, charts, graphs, and explanatory text. That requires operational capability to prepare publication-ready statistical outputs and respond to enquiries about program results. The Operations Officer is relevant because the role 'Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications' and 'Responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.' While the role is more operationally centered on collection/coding/processing, these explicit publication and user-information duties directly support dissemination activities.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because dissemination products must be prepared for user consumption and often require reporting, visualization, and communication of valid, reliable data in forms suitable for decision-makers and clients. That requires capability in data preparation, validation, visualization, and producing analytical reports and dashboards. The Junior Data Analyst is relevant because the role conducts 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and has knowledge covering 'summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence.' The role also notes that 'Writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients' and to develop 'briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data.' These functions support dissemination-ready outputs, even if the role is not a primary dissemination role.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Update output systems
description: This sub-process manages the update of output systems and databases for dissemination using automated, real-time loading of data and enriched metadata. Machine-actionable formatting, digital linkage, and metadata validation are built-in, ensuring that all disseminated products are AI- and API-consumable, searchable, and enriched with discoverability standards. Final checks for completeness and metadata enrichment are automatic, and all outputs are designed for seamless use by both human and digital consumers.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly concerns updating dissemination systems and databases with automated loading, metadata enrichment, metadata validation, and output readiness for digital consumption. That requires capability to produce, edit, validate, store and disseminate statistical metadata, assess metadata quality, and support changes to metadata methods and systems. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository,' and 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems.' The role also has knowledge of 'methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata' and analyzes changes 'to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats,' which directly matches machine-actionable formatting, metadata validation, and enriched dissemination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it manages dissemination output systems and databases, including final automated checks, loading of data, and ensuring disseminated products are usable by clients and digital consumers. That requires capability in editing, validating, reviewing data quality from systems and databases, disseminating data, and interpreting user needs for outputs. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' and 'participates on data production and dissemination teams.' The role also 'compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output,' 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' and 'adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats,' which aligns closely with updating output systems for dissemination and ensuring outputs are complete and fit for use.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because updating output systems and dissemination databases with automated loading and machine-actionable outputs requires operational support for processing systems, database maintenance and conversion, and assessment of how output changes affect integrity and completeness. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and has contextual knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, general software packages and computer languages, for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.' The role also 'analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results,' which directly supports updating dissemination systems and final completeness checks.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because machine-actionable formatting, automated loading, searchable/API-consumable outputs, and validation of dissemination-ready data require data preparation, transformation, cleansing, validation, and conformity to standards. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' The role also requires knowledge of the data science life cycle including 'data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, ... summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence,' which supports the technical preparation of outputs and databases for automated dissemination environments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because updating output systems for dissemination requires translating subject-matter requirements into system specifications, assessing effects of procedural and technology changes on outputs, and improving presentation methods. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role 'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development,' and in research and analysis 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' The role also 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems,' which is directly relevant to updating dissemination outputs and systems.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Produce dissemination products
description: This sub-process produces dissemination outputs using automated, AI- and LLM-powered workflows to generate, assemble, and format all products—including publications, press releases, online tables, interactive graphics, maps, and PUMFs—as standard. Text, graphics, and narrative products are created with digital automation as first resort, and all products (including mandatory PUMFs) are checked for standards adherence by human specialists, who refine outputs and ensure audience appropriateness as required. All dissemination outputs are machine-actionable, metadata-enriched, and ready for instant digital release.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is explicitly about producing and disseminating statistical outputs in multiple formats—"publications, press releases, online tables, interactive graphics, maps, and PUMFs"—and ensuring they are refined and ready for release. That requires a role able to disseminate data, create output products, interpret user needs, and adapt outputs into appropriate presentation formats. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills this need because the role "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," and "Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output." It is also specifically aligned to formatting and tailoring dissemination products because it "Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats" and drafts material "included in publications."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because all dissemination outputs must be "machine-actionable, metadata-enriched, and ready for instant digital release." That creates a direct need for production, validation, dissemination, and quality evaluation of statistical metadata so products can be properly described, discoverable, and standards-compliant. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository." The work description also directly matches the standards and metadata-enrichment requirement through "knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks," participation in "the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata," and assistance with "statistical metadata quality evaluations."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination products include structured outputs such as "online tables, interactive graphics, maps" and require automated generation, assembly, formatting, and validation for audience use. That requires capability in preparing data, ensuring conformity to standards, and producing visual and analytical outputs. The Junior Data Analyst helps meet this need because the role "Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." It also supports dissemination-ready products through knowledge of "reporting, visualization, business intelligence" and the ability to develop "briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination products must be assembled into publication-ready forms, including tables, charts, graphs, and explanatory text, and checked for quality and appropriateness before release. That requires a role experienced in preparing publication components and understanding output quality. The Operations Officer is directly relevant because the role "Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications." The role also supports standards adherence and release-readiness through knowledge of "methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications" and by responding to enquiries on "the use of program results."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because dissemination outputs include analytical and publication-oriented material, and human specialists must refine outputs and ensure they are appropriate for users and publication. That requires subject-matter analysis, preparation of analytical material for publication, and attention to presentation methods. The Economist/Sociologist 2 is implicated because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes." The work description also directly connects to dissemination presentation needs by noting participation in feedback on "presentation methods and procedures" and knowledge needed to adhere to practices involved in the "presentation of statistical data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Release dissemination products
description: This sub-process releases dissemination products using digital automation to handle all elements of release—timing, briefing, embargo, subscriber access, and confidential data management. Orchestration platforms schedule, log, and manage real-time releases. Human staff review and approve exception cases, interact with high-level subscribers, and handle policy or retraction scenarios as required, ensuring transparency and compliance at all times.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is specifically about releasing dissemination products and managing the operational, client-facing, and compliance aspects of that release, including subscriber access and confidential data management. It therefore needs a role that directly performs dissemination of statistical outputs, responds to user requests, and works within the legal and policy framework governing release. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer directly fills that need because the role "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data," "Provides statistical data and consultative services to users," and "Participates on data production and dissemination teams." The work-description also shows release-relevant analytical and client service capability through "Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required." For compliance during release, the role explicitly requires "Knowledge of the Statistics Act ... and of Statistics Canada policies ... in the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data" and awareness of "the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because release of dissemination products includes not only data release but also the release of supporting metadata, with automation, quality control, and compliance around dissemination. It therefore needs a role that prepares and disseminates metadata, supports dissemination systems and procedures, and ensures confidentiality and policy compliance. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository." The role also supports dissemination operations by providing "feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata" and participating "in the testing of new procedures and systems." This aligns with automated orchestration and release platforms. For compliance and confidentiality in release, the work-description explicitly cites "Knowledge of policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata" and states that the position must have awareness of "the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because release dissemination products require preparation of statistical outputs for publication, interaction with users, and handling dissemination-related products and services in a way that preserves consistency and confidentiality. It therefore needs subject-matter support for analytical material intended for publication and assistance to users. The Economist/Sociologist 2 is implicated because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes" and "Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada." Those duties support briefing, subscriber interaction, and release-ready analytical products. The role is also tied to dissemination-stage compliance because it requires knowledge of Statistics Canada policies and "particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data" in the "presentation of statistical data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated release requires operational control of systems and processes, management reporting, and handling of outputs in regular and ad-hoc publications, while ensuring confidentiality and reliable execution. It therefore needs an operations-oriented role that supports automated processes, prepares publication outputs, and responds to enquiries about program results. The Operations Officer fills part of that need because the role "Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," which is relevant to the automated orchestration environment described in the phase. The role also "Responds orally and in writing to enquiries ... to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results" and "Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications." For release control and compliance, the work-description includes knowledge of systems, data flows, and explicit awareness of "the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Promote dissemination products
description: This sub-process promotes statistical products using AI/automation-driven tools to generate, recommend, and deploy messaging across all platforms—web, email, social, and beyond. Content, format, and strategy are tailored with AI for each target audience, adjusting to maximize reach and impact. Staff intervene for high-level campaign review, optimization, and the management of complex or sensitive outreach.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: What makes this sub-process implicating is that it is explicitly about promoting dissemination products across channels and tailoring messaging, format and strategy to audiences in order to maximize reach and impact. This requires roles that directly support dissemination and marketing of statistical outputs, prepare explanatory content for users, and help communicate statistical products appropriately. This work-description fits that need most directly because it explicitly includes responsibility to "edit, validate, market and disseminate data," which aligns exactly with promotion of dissemination products. It also supports outreach content because the role "drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used" and provides "statistical data and consultative services to users," all of which are directly relevant to creating and supporting promotional messaging for dissemination products.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: What makes this sub-process implicating is that promotion of dissemination products depends not only on the data product itself but also on the metadata and descriptive information that help audiences discover, understand and use the product across dissemination platforms. This requires capability to prepare, validate and disseminate metadata, adapt it to formats and systems, and support dissemination quality. This work-description fills that need because it explicitly "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata" and has knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata." The role also "analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats," which is directly relevant when promotional content is deployed across web, email, social and other channels.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: What makes this sub-process implicating is that AI-driven promotion requires audience-tailored messaging, reporting, visualization and communication products that can be optimized for reach and impact. This creates a need for roles that can organize information, produce analytical material, and communicate findings through reports, presentations and visual outputs for varied audiences.
