This work-description supports that need because it includes "writing skills ... to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science." It also states that "data literacy includes ... visualize and communicate data" and that the role supports reporting and visualization as part of the data science life cycle, including "summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence." Those capabilities are directly useful for preparing and optimizing promotional dissemination content.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: What makes this sub-process implicating is that promoting dissemination products often requires preparing analytical material for publication purposes, identifying trends worth highlighting, and translating technical subject matter into accessible content for users and audiences. This requires subject-matter support for publication-oriented communication. This work-description fills that need because it "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes" and "identifies statistical trends and developments." It also "writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications," which is directly relevant to crafting understandable promotional messaging for dissemination products.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: What makes this sub-process implicating is that promotion across platforms can involve preparing publication-ready tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text that support dissemination outputs and outreach materials. This requires operational capability to produce presentation-ready statistical content and explain program results to users and the public. This work-description contributes to that need because it "designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications" and "responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results." While its core focus is operations, these publication and public-information functions are directly supportive of promoting dissemination products.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Provide user support
description: This sub-process provides user support through AI-powered chatbots and automation interfaces, which record, triage, and answer user queries in real time, guiding users to datasets, data interpretations, and publications as needed. Complex inquiries and escalations go to human staff for resolution, especially for nuanced, sensitive, or high-value support. User feedback and request tracking are used to populate knowledge bases and feed into service quality improvement.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on answering user queries, guiding users to datasets and interpretations, and handling escalated requests that require human resolution. That requires staff who can interpret user information requests, provide consultative services, and disseminate statistical outputs appropriately. This work-description directly fits that need because it explicitly states that the role "Provides statistical data and consultative services to users," "Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations," and "Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data." Those duties align closely with real-time support, guidance to data products, and resolution of more complex user requests.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because user support depends not only on directing users to datasets, but also on guiding them to the right metadata, documentation, and explanatory material, while feeding knowledge bases and improving service quality. That requires capability in producing, validating, disseminating, and advising on metadata and documentation. This work-description fills that need because it "Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata," and contributes to "documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals." It also "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations," which supports the sub-process requirement that feedback and request tracking populate knowledge bases and improve service quality.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because complex user inquiries often require human staff who can provide data assistance, explain outputs, and support interpretation for internal and external users. That requires subject-matter staff able to assist users and translate technical concepts into understandable terms. This work-description meets that need because it explicitly says the role "Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada," and "participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes." It also includes writing and presenting "technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications," which is directly relevant to nuanced support and interpretation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because user support channels must respond to enquiries, explain processes and results, and support users when questions concern operational systems, collection processes, or program results. That requires staff able to answer enquiries orally and in writing and explain technical procedures clearly. This work-description fills that need because it states the role "Responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results." It also notes contact with respondents and others "to clarify problems or irregularities" and to "clarify and explain statistical concepts," which is directly relevant to escalated support cases.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because effective user support includes helping users interpret data correctly, providing guidance to data users and clients, and communicating analytical information in ways that minimize misinterpretation. That requires staff with data literacy, communication skills, and the ability to advise users on data use and governance. This work-description supports that need because it says the role "Provides advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets." It also requires writing "clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material... for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science" and presenting information so as "to minimize the potential for misinterpretation," which is highly relevant to user support and data interpretation guidance.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because user feedback and request tracking are used to improve service quality, which creates a need to gather, analyze, and synthesize qualitative and quantitative information about user needs, requirements, and service performance. This work-description is relevant because it includes conducting research, gathering and analyzing data, participating in interviews and focus groups, and supporting assessments of current and future data requirements. Specifically, it "undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as... identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups," and "Provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data." Those capabilities align with analyzing support feedback and informing service improvement, even if the role is less directly involved in frontline user support than dissemination roles.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

title: Evaluate
description: This phase manages evaluation for each statistical business process instance using automation and AI/LLM-powered pipelines for gathering, synthesizing, and analyzing all feedback and performance metrics. Iterative, digital-first workflows continuously update and surface actionable insights, with automated reports and dashboards flagging opportunities for adjustment, learning, and quality enhancement. Human analysts focus on contextual review, recommendation adjudication, and final sign-off of improvement plans for future iterations. Evaluation may occur at the end or during any process cycle, and is broken into three sub-processes (Figure 14) which may run simultaneously or be repeated until required standards are met.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because it explicitly manages evaluation by gathering, synthesizing, and analyzing feedback and performance metrics, then turning findings into actionable insights and improvement plans. That requires capability in formal evaluation studies, qualitative and quantitative evidence gathering, synthesis, interpretation, and support to reporting and recommendations. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies," "identify[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," "apply[ies] analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulat[es] conclusions," and "provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because evaluation depends on analyzing performance metrics, producing dashboards and reports, and surfacing opportunities for adjustment and quality enhancement. That requires data preparation, quality assessment, statistical analysis, reporting, visualization, and support to decision-making. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods," conducts "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality," and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence" and the ability to develop "briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because evaluation includes reviewing operational performance metrics and identifying opportunities for adjustment in ongoing or completed process cycles. That requires assessing methods, procedures, results, and system requirements, and reporting operational problems and alternatives. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results," and "analyses reported data and work results" while preparing reports that present findings on implementation problems and recommend alternatives.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because evaluation requires contextual review of statistical program performance and recommendations for improvements to methods and procedures for future iterations. That requires subject-matter analysis of trends, assessment of methodological effects, and feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation, and presentation practices. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data," "suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and assists "in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." The role also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because evaluation includes assessing output quality, interpreting findings for users and managers, and identifying effects of procedural or system changes on products and services. That requires reviewing data quality, compiling and evaluating outputs, and supporting reports and improvement actions. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "compiles data from diverse sources," "summarizes and describes meaning of data," and "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." The role also "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This phase is implicating because evaluation in a statistical business process also includes assessing the quality and adequacy of metadata that supports interpretation, reuse, and quality enhancement across iterations. That requires metadata quality evaluation, analysis of methods and systems, and reporting on results for management improvement. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management," "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata," and "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Gather evaluation inputs
description: Evaluation input gathering is orchestrated via automated, AI/LLM-powered systems that harvest, aggregate, and cluster all feedback, process-metadata, quality metrics, and staff input in real time. Inputs are continuously updated and synthesized for use in ongoing and cyclical evaluation phases, easing the workload on evaluators and ensuring the highest possible input quality and completeness for downstream analysis and decision-making.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it is specifically about gathering and synthesizing evaluation inputs such as feedback, quality metrics, process information, and staff input for later evaluation use. That requires capability to identify, gather, analyze and synthesize qualitative and quantitative evaluation data from multiple sources. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fills that need because the role "undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups" and also "provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly includes harvesting and aggregating process-metadata and quality metrics as evaluation inputs. That requires capability to compile, validate, store, disseminate and evaluate metadata quality, and to interpret requirements for metadata-related inputs. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata," "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations," and "compiles information from diverse sources in order to prepare, edit, validate and evaluate statistical metadata." The role also has knowledge of "methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the phase description emphasizes automated, AI/LLM-powered harvesting, aggregation, clustering, and continuous synthesis of inputs in real time. That requires data lifecycle, data preparation, clustering, quality assessment, and analytical support capabilities suited to automated input pipelines. The Junior Data Analyst fills that need because the role supports studies using established analysis software and conducts "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin." The role's knowledge explicitly includes the data science life cycle, including "data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization" and "text mining, and qualitative analysis," which closely matches the automated harvesting and clustering aspects of this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because gathering evaluation inputs in real time depends on operational collection and processing streams that can supply reliable data, feedback, and process results. That requires capability in collection operations, evaluating methods and results, and analyzing impacts on integrity and completeness. The Operations Officer fills that need because the role "participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data," "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results," and "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results." These functions directly support the gathering of operational and process inputs into evaluation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because evaluation input gathering includes collecting and analyzing statistical program data and generating feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures. That requires subject-matter analysis of data and procedural impacts so that meaningful inputs can feed evaluation. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills that need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data," "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and has research responsibilities to "analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems."
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because the phase requires aggregation of quality metrics and other data inputs from diverse sources, with synthesis into usable outputs for downstream evaluation and decision-making. That requires compiling, validating, assessing quality, and interpreting data from multiple systems and sources. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills that need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases" and "compiles data from diverse sources" while "analyz[ing] and evaluat[ing] data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness." Those responsibilities directly support assembling high-quality evaluation inputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Conduct evaluation
description: This sub-process analyzes evaluation inputs using LLM/AI-powered digital evaluation algorithms. Automated benchmarking, synthesis, and reporting produce dashboards, quality issues lists, and draft improvement recommendations for each statistical production iteration. Human experts review AI-generated outputs, contextualize findings, and finalize the recommendations and improvement plans to be carried out in current or future cycles.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it centers on analyzing evaluation inputs, synthesizing quantitative and qualitative evidence, producing draft findings and recommendations, and then having human experts review and finalize improvement plans. That requires evaluation-specific analytical capability, ability to interpret evidence, formulate conclusions, and support reporting. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fits this need because the role "participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies," "identify[ies], gather[s], analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," applies "analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulat[e] conclusions," and "provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda." These duties align closely with AI-assisted evaluation analysis, synthesis, reporting, and final recommendation development.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because automated evaluation outputs include dashboards, benchmarking, synthesis, and draft recommendations, all of which depend on strong data analysis, data quality assessment, and reporting/visualization support before human review can finalize findings. That requires capability in preparing, validating, analyzing, and presenting data outputs. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role "supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software," performs "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality," and has knowledge of the data science life cycle including "summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence" and the ability to develop "briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data." This directly supports AI-enabled evaluation analysis and dashboard production.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because evaluation outputs must identify quality issues, assess consistency and reliability, and support draft improvement recommendations for statistical production iterations. That requires analytical review of data outputs and the ability to assess impacts of procedural or system changes on products and services. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fits this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "compiles data from diverse sources," "analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness," and "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services." Those responsibilities directly support evaluation of production results and identification of improvements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because human experts must review AI-generated findings, contextualize them, assess trends and issues in statistical production, and help finalize recommendations for future cycles. That requires subject-matter analytical capacity and the ability to assess methods and propose improvements. The Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of statistical program data," "identifies statistical trends and developments," "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures," and "assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." It also "analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems," which is directly relevant to contextualizing evaluation outputs and finalizing improvement plans.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because evaluation of a statistical production iteration must surface operational quality issues and recommend improvements to collection, coding, and processing procedures. That requires operational knowledge of methods, results, and alternatives. The Operations Officer fits this need because the role "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," "analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered... and recommending alternatives," and "analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results." These duties directly support identifying quality issues and improvement actions during evaluation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because evaluation may include assessing metadata-related quality issues and producing reports that inform improvement recommendations for future production cycles. That requires capability to evaluate metadata quality, analyze methods and systems, and contribute to reporting for management. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management," "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata," and "analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives." This is directly relevant where evaluation findings concern metadata quality and related process improvements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Agree an action plan
description: This sub-process brings together digital and AI-supported platforms for drafting, recommending, and monitoring action plans based on the synthesized evaluation. Automated dashboards and traceable tracking systems surface plan effectiveness and support human decision-makers in approving, customizing, and finalizing future improvement actions. Ongoing digital monitoring ensures that the impacts of each action feed directly into subsequent evaluation cycles, creating a robust loop of continuous improvement.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it focuses on drafting, recommending, approving, customizing, finalizing, and monitoring action plans based on evaluation findings. That requires capability to interpret evaluation evidence, determine implications of results, formulate conclusions, and provide material that supports management decision-making on future improvements. The Junior Evaluation Officer directly fills this need because the role "participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies," "analyz[es] and synthesiz[es] quantitative and qualitative data," applies tools "to determine implications of evaluation results and formulat[e] conclusions," and "provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management." Those duties directly support the recommendation and agreement of improvement actions arising from evaluation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because it explicitly relies on "digital and AI-supported platforms," "automated dashboards," and "traceable tracking systems" to monitor action-plan effectiveness and feed results into future evaluation cycles. That requires capability to prepare reliable data inputs, assess data quality, support dashboards and presentations, and organize information for ongoing monitoring. The Junior Data Analyst fills this need because the role supports studies using quantitative analysis tools, conducts "data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality," and has knowledge needed to develop "briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data." The role also participates in project teams supporting "data management, research and analysis," which aligns with maintaining evidence for action-plan tracking and continuous improvement.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because agreeing an action plan requires assessing operational effectiveness, identifying where procedures should change, and recommending alternatives that can be implemented and monitored over time. That creates a need for operational analysis, reporting on results, and recommendations on methods and procedures. The Operations Officer fills this need because the role "evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives," "prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems," and "analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists... recommending alternatives." Those responsibilities directly support the formulation and operationalization of improvement actions and their subsequent monitoring.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because action plans must be based on synthesized findings and translated into concrete program improvements, with priorities, target dates, and procedural modifications that can be approved and tracked. That requires analytical capacity to assess impacts of current methods and propose changes to ongoing programs. Economist/Sociologist 2 fills this need because the role "participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities." It also liaises with others "to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates." These are directly aligned with agreeing and structuring an action plan for improvement.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because action plans depend on evidence about data outputs, service impacts, and the effects of procedural or system changes, and they often require communicating findings and improvement options to users and managers. That creates a need to assess data quality, analyze impacts of changes, and support dissemination of evidence used in decision-making. The Data Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases," "provides statistical data and consultative services to users," and "analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services." The role also drafts reports on "the interpretation and use of statistical data," which supports evidence-based approval and customization of action plans.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process is implicating because continuous improvement loops and traceable monitoring require clear documentation of methods, procedures, standards, and quality information so that agreed actions can be tracked and evaluated consistently over subsequent cycles. That creates a need for maintaining and evaluating metadata and documenting procedural changes. The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer fills this need because the role "provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata," "participates in the testing of new procedures and systems," and "assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management." The role also contributes to "documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals," which supports traceable implementation and monitoring of agreed actions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
